item.description:
1.0.18 (build 5191)   Nov 19, 2026   This version

New

  • Panels you arrange as you work. Drag any panel's tab and a cross lights over the pane under the pointer: let go on the middle to join it as a tab, on an arrow to split the pane, or on the targets at the window's edges to dock it along a whole edge. Let go outside the window and the panel floats, and floating windows take other panels too, so several can float together; Dock puts them back. Every pane's title bar has a collapse arrow: the pane folds to a slim rail on its nearest window edge, its panels named on it, and a click on a name brings it back in its own place and size (or press ⇧Space over a pane, and over the rail). Space still fills the window with a panel. Each workspace keeps your arrangement as you work, and Window > Workspaces > Reset this workspace puts Kento's back. The Viewer, Node Graph and Curve Editor float alone, each in a window of its own. Layouts you saved before open as docks.
  • Connecting nodes far apart in the Node Graph. Click a port (without dragging) and a new wire stays on the pointer, with a label naming what you hold, while you scroll, zoom, pan, frame or find; click an input to connect it, or a node's body for its free input (a short menu asks when a Merge's B and A are both free). Shift-click connects and keeps the wire, Esc or a click on empty ground drops it. A wire you drag or carry near the graph's edge slides the graph that way. J connects the selection, the node picked last taking the others in the order you picked them, and right-clicking a port lists the comp's nodes to connect it to, found as you type (⇧J for the selected node's input). Each connection is one undo, and loops are refused with the usual card. Change the keys in Settings > Keyboard.
  • The Dope Sheet's side columns fold out of the way, in every mode. A chevron at the top of each column folds it to a slim rail with its name written up it: the names in Keys and Footage, and in Edit mode Media, Media's Sources column and the track headers. Click the rail to bring the column back at the width it had (the names and Media can also be dragged out of the rail to a new width), or press \ to fold or open the column under the pointer (change the key in Settings > Keyboard). Keys and Footage keep their own names' fold and width, and Kento remembers every column's fold and width in its settings, so the Dope Sheet opens as you left it. ⇧⌘M still hides Media altogether. The fold slides for a moment, unless the system's Reduce motion is on.
  • Named links: a Send under a plate, a camera or anything used all over a big comp, and Receives anywhere else carry its picture with no wire drawn across the graph. Right-click a node's output (or choose Edit > Node > Send from here) to make a Send; a new Receive asks which Send by name from a menu. Each tile shows the link's name; selecting one outlines its partners with a faint dashed line to each, and Go to linked node (⌥J) jumps between them. Renaming a Send keeps its Receives linked; deleting it leaves its Receives saying no sender, with Choose a Send... to fix it. They carry 3D scenes and cameras too, cost nothing to render, and are saved in .ko and .nk files.

Improved

  • Kento gives memory back to your other apps. Left quiet for 15 seconds, it hands back the memory its render engine kept for reuse; left alone for 5 minutes, or a minute behind another app, its caches shrink to 1 GB each until your next click or key; when macOS runs short of memory it shrinks them at once. Its hash cache is also half the size it was, with no loss of speed. On a Mac Studio after the same work on two 4K show comps, Kento held 8.6 to 12.6 GB instead of about 20. The limits will keep changing as we measure on smaller Macs (Settings > Speed and memory).
  • Playing a comp while its playback cache fills is faster: Kento no longer reads the next frames' files ahead while it plays (the playback cache works those frames out itself, and each frame change waited for the read ahead it cancelled). A 4K show comp on a 16 GB Mac mini: 0.5 to 0.8 frames a second.
  • Playing a comp whose picture carries other layers (mattes, passes, depth) beside its colors: the playback cache now works out only the channels the Viewer shows, so it fills about twice as fast on a 16 GB Mac mini and nearly three times as fast on a larger Mac at full size (a 4K show comp: 0.23 to about 0.5 frames a second on the mini, 0.19 to 0.55 at full size), and plays from the cache two to three times as fast, with the same pictures.
  • Nuke comps that use the link add-on (anchor and wired nodes, often called Stamps) open with each anchor as a Send and each wired node as a Receive, named for the anchor's title, with the same picture; the import says how many links were made, and a saved .nk holds Kento's own Send and Receive groups.

Fixed

  • Render now starts the render on this Mac too (it queued the frames and waited). A render node sends the image files back to the Mac that sent the job.
  • Kento no longer crashes as it quits. After its last window closed, tearing down what the session still held could crash the app on its way out; Kento now finishes its work (settings, starting values, the remote door) and ends cleanly.
  • Kento's remote control can run a menu command that needs its comp's window (Kento > Quit failed before).
  • Python scripts that sample a picture (and Kento's own tools that read a pixel) no longer freeze Kento on comps whose nodes run Python expressions, such as the studio's keyed comps.
  • Comps numbered from eight-digit frames (timecode numbering, 86400000 on): Perspective's line sets show and go to their real frame numbers, and a retime node left at its default frame range no longer stops the comp's range moving to eight digits.
  • Option and an arrow key nudge the points picked in the Viewer (a panel's corners and handles, Roto, GridWarp and SplineWarp points) with the pointer over the Viewer. Before, the Viewer took them as Option-Right and Option-Left, jumping to the next or previous key; with nothing picked they still do.
  • A key with a black clean plate (IBKGizmoV3 over a plate with no screen) no longer fills the picture with NaN pixels, which a following blur spread; it keeps the color with full alpha, as NukeX does.
  • Optimize lists a faster compatibility swap only when it saves a quarter of the time of what it replaces, as its measuring decides, so every card says what the swap does to the picture (a marginal one was listed with nothing said).

Earlier updates

1.0.17 (build 5056)   Nov 18, 2026

New

  • Hide overlays on the Viewer's second bar (⇧O, which you can change in Settings > Keyboard): the picture alone, without the open panels' on-screen controls, outlines and labels, the picks and the annotations, with every panel left open (the notes saying a file is missing or a render failed stay). While it's on, the button is solid blue with a white icon and an Overlays hidden pill shows in the Viewer's corner (click it to show them again). The hidden controls don't respond to clicks, drags or keys; you can still pan and zoom.

Improved

  • The Viewer's Paused and Working at notes are now see-through pills over the picture, with a small colored light for the state (red for paused) instead of a solid block, and a tooltip saying what a click does.
  • Save, Save as... and Save new version say what they saved: a short note under the Timeline (Saved as BOU180_comp_v003.ko) with Show in Finder, fading by itself. A comp's name in the note shows at once which comp was saved.
  • A node's panel has Reset all to defaults on its header (the round arrow left of the Presets button), one undo; it was only in the Presets menu, which still has it.
  • A saturation slider's track (ColorCorrect, Grade, HSVTool, Saturation and the other color nodes) runs from gray to one full color, so it shows how much color, not which; it swept through several hues before and read as a hue control.
  • Rename in the file dialog as in the Finder: click the name of the item already chosen, wait a moment, and it opens for typing (Return keeps the name, Esc leaves it; a double-click still opens). F2 still renames.
  • Batch rename and renumber in the file dialog. Right-click a numbered run for Rename... or Renumber...: a new name (the shot's name is offered when Kento knows the shot), the start frame and the padding, gaps kept unless you choose to close them, and a preview before anything changes. Several files take Rename N items: replace text, add text, or a name with a counter. Every file is renamed or none is, a card offers Undo, and when the comp's Reads use the old names it offers to point them at the new ones.
  • Kento's file dialog chooses several files at once: ⌘-click, ⇧-click and ⌘A, in the list and in a column, a numbered run of frames counting as one; the button says how many (Bring in 5). The Media panel's Bring in now uses it in place of the system's dialog, and so do importing lens files and a lens's grid images.
  • The file dialog's right-click menu, in the list and the columns: a line saying what the item is, then Open, Show in Finder, Copy path, Add to favorites, Rename (F2), Move to Trash and New folder; below the items, the folder's own. A new folder's name opens for typing in place (Esc takes the empty folder away), Move to Trash shows a card whose Undo puts it back, and typing a name's first letters jumps to it in a column.
  • Every file and folder picker opens where it makes sense: at the folder of the file the control already holds (or the nearest folder above it, when that folder is gone), else where this node last chose from, else the last folder used for that kind of thing (footage, renders, comps, LUTs, 3D and so on, kept with your preferences), else the comp's folder, else home. This covers every node's Browse, the footage browser, Open, Save, Import, Export, the Media panel's Bring in and the settings' folders; a few pickers that still used the system's dialog now use Kento's.
  • Type a path in the file dialog and the footage browser: ⌘L, a click on the path or typing / or ~ opens the field, a list shows the names that match, Tab finishes the name, Return goes there or chooses the file, and a Windows or Linux path is read through the path maps. The footage browser has the field for the first time.
  • The file dialog and the footage browser have a column view like the Finder's: each folder a column, the preview as the last, sequences as one item, the arrow keys moving between columns. A button beside the star switches between list and columns, and the choice is remembered.
  • Highlight Rebuild's sliders fit how it is used, and a graph shows whether it is doing anything. softness runs the node's whole 0 to 0.5 and radius 0 to 300 px, both with the small values given the room (marks at 0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.2, 0.5 and 0, 10, 50, 100, 300). Under Clipping, a strip shows the top end of the picture in red, green and blue before (filled) and after (outlined) the rebuild, so the pile-up at the clip and its spread above it are both visible, the clip level as a line and the weight that counts a value as clipped as a curve rising to it: drag the line to set clipped at, the curve's foot to set softness. A line under it says how much of the frame is being rebuilt (for example "Rebuilding 3.2% of the frame (R 2.1, G 0.4, B 1.0)") or that nothing is clipped at the level set and how bright the picture goes, and a note says to set clipped at just below where the plate clips (the usual reason it looks like it does little). strength says what it is: how much of the rebuilt highlight replaces the clipped one, 0 to 1.
  • A number typed past its slider's range no longer leaves the slider stuck at its end, on every node: where the knob has no limit there the slider stretches to show it (radius 450 shows a slider to 500), and where the knob stops (strength at 1) the field shows the value the knob holds. Stored values are not changed.

Fixed

  • With two comps open, an item chosen from the menu bar (or by its keys) could act on the other comp, not the one in front: Save new version saved the comp behind. Every menu item now acts on the comp in front, and an item that fails says so in its window.
  • A Write's Browse button opened a dialog for choosing a file that already exists, with nowhere to type a name. It now asks for the name to render to, with the Write's own name, frame numbers and extension filled in; a folder that isn't made yet is kept.
  • A Read with a missing file no longer makes its red error card flash. The card at the top of its panel (and the red edge on its tile) was made again every time the Viewer asked for another piece of the picture; it is now made once, stays put, and changes only when the words change (another file name, the missing frames setting) or the file comes back.
  • A big picture shown zoomed out in the Viewer (a UHD plate at 25 or 50%, even at Full working resolution) no longer looks jagged and shimmering: the Viewer now averages the pixels each screen pixel covers, as other image viewers do, and the frames held for playback are shown the same way. At 100% and above pixels are still shown as sharp squares. Renders and the pixel readout are unchanged.
1.0.16 (build 5031)   Nov 18, 2026

New

  • A new node, To ACEScg, in the Generative menu, brings generated video, web pictures and client stills into an ACEScg comp the right way. Pick what the image is in What is it?, with a line under the menu saying what each choice assumes: Generated video or web image (sRGB) (the right choice for most generated media), Video from a camera or edit (Rec.709), the Rec.709 camera curve for footage that really is scene light, Match the Viewer exactly so it shows as it did in a browser, Already linear Rec.709 and Already ACEScg. Guess from the file reads the movie's or picture's color tags and picks for you, saying why (a movie tagged Rec.709 that a video generator such as Seedance, Runway, Kling, Sora or Veo made is taken as sRGB, as generated video is), and sorts out a Read that was converting the file too. Alpha stays as it is. It runs through your comp's color config, or the same math built in when the config hasn't the spaces; the render engine does the same, it is saved with the comp, and a Nuke script gets a group of Nuke's own color nodes doing the same.
  • Nuke camera channel files (.chan) read and write. A Camera with a .chan file and Read from file keys its translate and rotate from the file, and its focal length from the vertical field of view column when the file has one; the Camera's own rotation order turns the numbers, as in Nuke. A Write Geo set to .chan writes the first camera in the scene, a line a frame with its translate, rotate and vertical field of view, and the file reads back as the same camera. Write Geo's file type menu has Camera channels (chan).
  • A Read's premultiplied works. Turn it on for a file whose color is already multiplied by its alpha (a premultiplied render, a ProRes 4444): the input transform divides the alpha out, converts the color, and multiplies it back, so the soft edges convert correctly. Off, the default, converts the values as they are. It is saved with the comp, read from a Nuke script, and the render engine does the same.

Improved

  • The color space menus are short now. A Read's input transform (and a Write's output transform, a Colorspace node's in and out, and the menu behind a Read's tag in the Node Graph) lists default, the comp's working space and the common spaces first: ACEScg, ACES2065-1, Linear Rec.709, sRGB, Rec.709, the Gamma ones, ARRI LogC3 and LogC4, S-Log3, Log3G10, V-Log, CanonLog3, Blackmagic Film Gen 5, DaVinci Intermediate and Raw, by the names your config gives them. The last five you chose are under Recent. Every other space is in a submenu for its family (Input, then ARRI, Sony or RED; Utility; ACES), with Other for spaces without one and Display for the display spaces. Type to find a space in any submenu. Comps and .nk files are unchanged.
  • A paused Viewer is easy to see now: while you have Pause updates on, its button turns solid red with a white icon, and the Paused chip in the Viewer's corner is solid red with white text. Both stay readable at every interface brightness.
  • A node's properties floated in a window of their own now look like the rest of Kento: the window is titled with the node's name, the panel fills it in Kento's dark look with no light gray frame, and it is as tall as its rows, with no empty strip under them. While a panel floats, the button in its header is Dock, which closes the window and puts the panel back at the top of the Properties bin.
  • A new workspace for cutting: Window > Workspaces > Edit puts the Viewer and Properties side by side across the top and the Dope Sheet across the whole width below them, already in Edit mode, with the Node Graph and Curve Editor as tabs beside it. The Compositing workspace is unchanged.

Fixed

  • A Viewer could show a black picture while everything behind it was right, with the Pause updates button lit and nothing saying it was paused. The button now shows only your own pause (not the pause the Viewer uses while it plays a held frame or while you drag in the 3D view), a paused Viewer shows a small Paused chip in its top right corner that un-pauses when you click it, and a Viewer paused before it has drawn anything draws one picture first and then holds it.
  • A movie in the Viewer at Half or Quarter (While playing, or a Viewer set to work smaller) showed in the wrong colors, a blue sky cyan and warm colors pink. It now looks the same at every size.
  • Edit mode's filmstrip showed a movie's frames in the same wrong colors. The frames now look as they do in the Viewer.
  • On a Read, premultiplied, raw data and auto alpha all showed gray as if they weren't built, and raw data and auto alpha couldn't be clicked in the panel (they shared a row with the not-yet premultiplied switch). The three are working switches on one row now. Raw data and auto alpha themselves were already right; note that a movie's pictures already have an alpha of 1, so auto alpha changes nothing on a movie.
  • The charts in the Utility menu (Color checker, Grey card, Color bars, Color wheel) made a node with no input or output. Each now shows its output port, wires into a Viewer or a Merge, draws its chart at the comp's format, and goes under the selected node as a node made with Tab does. Its panel says what it is (the checker lists its 24 patches by name), and it saves and opens again in a .ko or .nk. Any group made empty and given its output afterward shows its ports now too.
1.0.15 (build 4995)   Nov 18, 2026

New

  • A working resolution: Kento works the comp out at the size your screen can show while you work, and at full when you stop. Settings, Performance, Working resolution sets it for every Viewer: While you work (Auto, Full, Half or Quarter), While playing, While dragging a control, and When you stop (Full or Stay). Auto picks the smallest size that still fills the Viewer's real pixels, so a 4K plate in a Viewer on a 1x display works at Half, and on a Retina display at Full; when it picks a smaller size, a small card by the Viewer says so and fades. Stopped for a couple of seconds, the frame comes back at full. Renders and Writes are always full resolution. The Viewer's two Downscale menus are now one control on bar 2, with Auto, the sizes (Nuke's 1:2 and 1:4 beside them), While playing and Full resolution when stopped, and a chip in the Viewer's corner says the size it is working at. Settings, Performance opens with what Kento suggests for this Mac (from its memory, GPU, display and cache drive), with Use these and Keep mine, and a card says what was picked the first time Kento starts on a Mac. The disk cache keeps the Viewers' results as compressed half float (about a fifth of the size), depth and other data as full float, at the working size by default on a 16 GB Mac (Keep results at: Working size, Full size or Both side by side), is on by default on every Mac, and a frame you leave never waits for its results to be read back. Renders keep and read full-precision results only.
  • The Dope Sheet has an Edit mode. Click Edit at the start of its strip, beside Keys and Footage, and the comp's clips (Reads, TimeClips, AppendClips, a clip laid over a Merge) show as tracks, as an editor shows a cut. Trim where you point, as in an editor's trim mode: just left of a join ripples the clip's end, on the join rolls it, just right of it ripples the next clip's start, the upper half of a clip slips its frames and the lower half slides it between its neighbors. A chip names the trim as the pointer arrives. While you drag, a tag says what it does and what it snaps to, and the Viewer shows the frame before the edit and the frame after it side by side; let go and it is one undo. Cut at the playhead, change a clip's speed, reverse it, hold a frame, dissolve the joins (from each clip's handles, a red end where a clip has no more frames) and delete a clip closing the gap. Each clip keeps a history to go back to a step (Settings, Node Graph, Keep clip history). The keys are an editor's own (A, T, W, B, N, Shift+Cmd+L and the rest, listed in Settings, Shortcuts) and Keys mode keeps its own. Everything is written to the comp's own clip nodes, so the comp renders what you see, and a Nuke script keeps the trims, cuts, speeds and dissolves. A show's cut on a Cut node, snapshots, proxies while playing and comps on segments come later and show dim with what brings them.
  • Edit mode's clips know their versions. A clip whose file name has a version (v001, _v12) shows a chip saying which one plays and how many are on disk (v001 of 3), with a dot when a newer one has been written. Control+Option+Up and Control+Option+Down step the picked clips to the next version and the one before, Shift+Option+Up to the latest; click the chip for the list, with when each was made and by whom where known. A swap keeps the cut as it was, the same frames in the same places, and is one undo. A version that lacks frames the cut uses isn't swapped: a card by the clip says which frames are missing and offers Trim to fit or Keep the length. A clip can follow the latest version, taking each new one by itself with a Back on its notice; new clips stay on the version they came in with. All clips to their latest version updates the picked clips, or the whole timeline, in one undo and says what changed. Browse for a version takes any file, from another app or a vendor, marked external on the chip and kept in the clip's menu. Versions are found in the background, so a slow drive never holds up the edit.
  • Edit mode can take a version before all its frames are on disk. Wait for the frames keeps the clip's length and every frame in its place; frames that aren't there yet show a dark hatched picture naming the version and the frames ("Frames not on disk yet: v004, 1013 to 1016"), never black, and are hatched on the track, filling in by themselves as the files land. A clip following the latest version now takes a newer one this way even when it is short, and its card says which frames are still to come. Refresh this version (Control+Option+R) and Refresh all versions (Shift+Control+Option+R) read the files again, for a version picked up before its render finished. All clips to their latest version keeps external picks, and its card offers Move external picks too; the version menu has both. The edit's format: in a comp, the first clip into an empty edit sets the comp's format, with Back; a clip or version of another size or frame rate coming in later asks, listing its settings against the comp's, with Change to match, Keep current, Other... and Don't ask for this edit.
  • Edit mode has gaps, as an editor does. Delete takes the picked clip out and leaves empty track where it was, and nothing else moves. As in an editor, deleting from the timeline never removes the media: the clip's Read stays in the comp and shows under View, Reads not cut yet, ready to cut again; pick a gap and press Delete to close it, or use Shift+Delete (or Forward Delete) to take a clip out and close the gap at once. Trim a clip into a gap beside it, or ripple a gap shorter. With sync lock on, a track running across an edit that ripples gets a gap opened in it, or the same frames taken out, so what comes after stays in step. A gap is a black Constant in the comp, so a Nuke script plays black there. Insert, Overwrite, Append and Place on top are on the F keys, as in DaVinci Resolve.
  • Edit mode has Media, a bin docked at the left of its tracks (the strip's Media panel button, or Shift+Cmd+M). Its left column lists sources (this comp's Reads, its Reads not cut yet, folders and files brought in, an Asobi playlist file, the other open comps), show bins that every comp of the show shares, this comp's own bins (saved in the comp), and smart groups built from menus that update by themselves; Search every source finds a clip anywhere. Clips list one to a line, with their picture, kind, version, frames and marked in and out, or as thumbnails. Double-click a clip, or press Return, to see it in the Viewer as the source: mark its in and out with I and O (Option+X clears), and Q swaps back to the timeline. Get a clip in the way editors do: drag it onto a track (a plain drag overwrites, Cmd+Shift inserts, and a tag says what the drop will do), drag it over the Viewer and drop it on one of the edit overlay's zones, or use the seven edits, Insert (F9), Overwrite (F10), Replace (F11), Place on top (F12), Ripple overwrite (Shift+F10), Fit to fill (Shift+F11) and Append at end (Shift+F12), from the strip's buttons, the keys (the Kento key set adds G, H, C and P) or the Source viewer's buttons. Each drop is one undo, named in Edit, History. A drop that can't be made changes nothing and says why by the tracks, with a button that fixes it: a locked track (Unlock), missing files (Relink... or Drop it offline), Fit to fill with nothing marked (Mark the segment, X). Comps as clips that play their latest render, and the tracker's shots as a source, come later and show dim.
  • Every Edit mode command with a key can be given another one on the Shortcuts page (Settings, Keyboard, Dope Sheet, Edit mode), in either key set: the edits and their letters, the version and refresh keys, the trim keys and Esc to put a held trim back. Your key is kept through a change of key set and a restart. The version keys moved to Control+Option+Up and Down, and Refresh to Control+Option+R, because Option+Up and Down move clips a track up or down in DaVinci Resolve; in Edit mode those two now say that isn't in Kento yet.
  • Edit mode's keys come in two sets, chosen with Edit mode on the Shortcuts page (Settings, Keyboard). Resolve, the default, is DaVinci Resolve's own keys, so G, H, C and P don't do anything a Resolve editor wouldn't expect. Kento adds G, H, C and P for insert, overwrite, append and place on top, and Shift+Forward Delete for delete with ripple. Switching is instant and kept, and keys you set yourself stay on top of either set.
  • Edit mode's filmstrip and zoom now work as DaVinci Resolve's do. Every picture is 16:9 and as tall as the track, laid edge to edge with no lines, a frame of another shape filling it from the middle (cropped, never squeezed), so a taller track shows wider pictures and fewer of them and a clip's width sets how many it shows; zoomed in until a frame is wider than a picture, that frame repeats across its width, never squeezed. Track height is set for every video track with View, Track height... or Shift and the scroll wheel, and for one track by dragging its top edge in the headers. Every zoom keeps the playhead where it is on screen: Command-Equal and Command-Minus, a new zoom slider in the strip, the scroll wheel (Option too) and a pinch, stopping only at the timeline's start and end. View, Frame lines draws a faint line at each frame's edge (off at first), and View, Name below pictures puts the clip's name, kind and length in a bar under its pictures, as Resolve has them; by default the name stays over them.
  • In the Dope Sheet's Edit mode each clip now shows its own frames, as a strip of pictures along it with its name over them. Each picture is the frame that plays at that point in the cut, so a trimmed clip starts on its new first frame, a clip at 200% skips frames, a reversed one runs backwards and a frozen one repeats its frame. Zoom in for more of its frames. The pictures come in by themselves in the background, a gray tile while each is made, and never hold up trimming, scrolling or playback. View > Clips picks Filmstrip, Head and tail, Head only or Name only, and Settings keeps the choice.
  • ProofSheet, a contact sheet of Kento's own (Nodes menu, Merge). Pick what goes on the sheet instead of wiring a node for each picture: the wired inputs, frames of a clip (each cell read at its own frame, so one node shows a whole shot over time), its layers or its views. Situation presets set it up in one click. The cells fill the comp's format or a page size, 64 to a page, and a picture larger than its cell is averaged down so it keeps its detail. Labels with the fields you pick (frame, timecode, file name, layer, view) are drawn in the Viewer under the cells, never in the picture, or burned into it with a switch so they render. Frames are picked on a strip you drag, or typed. In the Viewer, hover a cell to see its file, frame and size; click to select it, double-click or press Return to see it alone ([ and ] step, Esc goes back), Shift-click a second cell to wipe the two, right-click for more, drag a cell to reorder the sheet; a selected cell has buttons and a time bar for a pen. A cell that can't be read says why and the rest of the sheet carries on. Borders can mark problems: missing frames, NaN, values below 0 or above 1. Made with several nodes selected, it takes them all as inputs in the order you picked them, and an order menu puts them by place in the Node Graph or by name instead. It renders on Kento's render engine. Nuke's ContactSheet stays in the toolbar. It can also show the comp's Reads, a folder of pictures, a shot's versions or a sequence's shots from the Shot panel, or an Asobi playlist in cut order (File, Import, Contact sheet as ProofSheet), with Use proxies to read small copies kept on the scratch drive. It can wedge one control across values, match its cells to a reference cell, and export to PDF and pictures (see Improved).
  • An eye on every section that changes the picture. Click the eye at the left of a section's header to turn that part of the node off and see the node without it; click again to turn it back on (one undo each). Press and hold it to see the node without the section only while you hold it. The section's values stay as you set them, a .ko keeps it off, and a Nuke script renders it on. Where Kento can't turn a section off yet, its eye is dim and its tip says why.
  • SmartMerge can glow A onto B: its new Glow section keys A's highlights by brightness, blurs them and screens them onto the background under A, at an amount. A glow input takes the glow from something other than A, such as A before a grade that dims its highlights. This does in one node what used to take a Keyer, a Premult, a Blur and a screen Merge.
  • You can now see and change where SmartMerge and Levels read the plate for a match. The part of the plate a match reads changes the result more than any setting, so the Viewer now outlines it while the panel is open, and a new read menu picks it: a narrow band round the element (where a new SmartMerge or Levels starts), around the element (what comps made before keep), around it without sky and foliage, its shade, its lit parts, or a box you drag. Drag the band's edge in the Viewer to widen it. After Measure, SmartMerge says how much of the plate it read and how far the element would move with each other choice; click one to take it.
  • Transform's Place first section has its own jack in the Viewer, smaller and dashed and named place, so you can drag an element into position while the node's own move stays the track. The section says when the element is placed and has Reset placement.
  • Difference's What changed section has presets: Regrain mask, Hard matte of any change and Soft change matte set its rows in one click.
  • SmartMerge's Glow section names what glows, draws where the glow starts and where it's full on a brightness scale you can drag, and shows a glow pill in the summary while it's on.
  • Difference can make a mask of what changed: its new What changed section cleans away specks, grows and softens the difference, and with hard 0 or 1 steps it at a threshold. A regrain's replace mask now takes one node instead of four. A .nk gets the same Nuke nodes in a Group.
  • Transform has a Place first section: place translate, rotate and scale move the input before the node's own move, filtered once with it. A match move's translate stays the track alone, so Roto shapes linked to it still follow the track, while the same node places the element. A .nk gets a Group of two Transforms.
  • ColorWheels: keep shadows at or above 0. A strong pull down or a lot of saturation could take the darkest shadows below 0; turn this on and no graded channel goes below 0. It's off by default, so comps graded before keep their look.

Improved

  • The Script Editor looks like something you can use. The input is a field that says how to run it (Cmd+Return, or Enter on the keypad; a selection runs alone), a slim row above has Run and Clear output, a line divides the output from the input, and the empty output offers three examples that paste into the input when clicked. Up on the input's first line brings back earlier commands and Down returns to what you were typing, kept for the session.
  • The Viewer is much faster on a comp with a motion-blurred Transform. Its motion blur is now worked out in one pass, as a render already did, instead of a full picture for each moment of the shutter. On a 16 GB Mac a heavy 4K comp went from about 34 seconds to 7 for a frame not seen yet, and no longer fills the memory. On a Mac with 16 GB of memory or less, Settings, Performance, Disk cache, Keep slow render results for later sessions now starts off: there, writing results to the disk and reading them back was slower than working them out. Turn it on to keep them anyway.
  • ProofSheet exports: a PDF of its pages for print (A4, Letter, A3 or Tabloid, either way up, with a header, a footer and a logo built from chips, previewed as it will print), or EXR, PNG and JPEG pictures, as the Viewer shows them or scene-linear. The labels go in the file whether or not they're burned into the picture. Send to Asobi writes the sheet with Asobi's own contact sheet file beside it, a still for each cell, for Asobi to open.
  • ProofSheet can match its cells to one another: set a reference cell in the Viewer, turn on Look, To the reference, and each cell's blacks and whites are carried to the reference's, all or part of the way. Exposure and warmth trim every cell at once. Only the pictures change, never the sheet's background, borders or labels, and the match is measured once and kept, so the sheet renders as fast as before.
  • ProofSheet can wedge a control: pick Wedge as what goes on the sheet, then a node and one of its controls, a range and how many steps (evenly or in even ratios). Each cell shows the picture with the control at one value, the values drawn under the range before anything renders and in the labels. The control is marked as linked and keeps its own value everywhere outside the sheet; right-click the cell you like and pick Take this value to keep it. Each change is one undo.
  • A ProofSheet of the comp's Reads, a folder, a shot's versions, a sequence's shots or an Asobi playlist now renders on Kento's render engine, as a sheet of wired inputs already did, with the same pixels. Its small copies (Use proxies) are made from the files your path maps point to, so a comp from another computer or from Windows works the same.
  • The Node Graph's tiles are now pale with dark names and dark family icons: easier to read, and the six families easier to tell apart, with any color vision and at any interface brightness. A selected tile goes paler inside its bold outline, with a thin dark gap between, and the yellow working edge and the red error edge sit just outside the tile where they show up. Prefer dark tiles? Settings > Node Graph > Node colors has Dark (classic), the tiles as they were, and two dark palettes with the families further apart. A color you gave a node stays, with its words dark or light to suit it.
  • Input labels in the Node Graph now sit right at their sockets and never wander. B, A and mask are always labeled, level, wired or not, and long names (matte, obj/scn) rise at an angle from the same spot; anything four letters or shorter stays level. Every wired input always shows with its label, as in other compositors: a Merge with A2 and up wired grows taller to hold them, and a MultiMerge with many wired layers grows wider. Only free inputs fold: a Merge's spare A inputs, a MultiMerge's free layers and layer masks, and a Viewer's free inputs share one socket with a count (+2) until you point at the node or bring a wire near; then they open, a Merge's on a small tab below its wired inputs, each with its own label. For a calmer graph, Settings > Node Graph > Fold Wired Inputs folds a busy node's wired extra inputs into that socket too. When the pointer leaves, they stay open for a moment so you can follow a wire, then fold back (Settings > Node Graph > Inputs Stay Open, 1.2 seconds). To keep a node's inputs open all the time, turn on keep inputs open in its Node tab, or select it and press Shift+H (Edit > Keep Inputs Open); the comp remembers it. A merge's operation (over, min) is now inside the tile with its name. Resting the pointer on an input says what it is for and where it comes from ("A2: laid over B with min", "From Grade3"), instead of an internal name, and a node's tooltip lists where its inputs come from.
  • The Node Graph's Viewer and MultiMerge follow the same inputs rule as every other node. A Viewer's input 1 always shows, its wired inputs show, and its other free inputs fold into one small socket with their count (+9 on a new Viewer); a wire dropped anywhere on an empty Viewer still goes to input 1. A MultiMerge's background and first layer always show, and a layer's mask input folds until it is wired.
  • Zooming the Node Graph no longer pops details in and out: names, icons, the words under tiles and the dots on wired ports fade over a few percent of zoom.
  • A failed node's red edge now stays while the node is still computing after an edit, however long that takes, so a slow node no longer flashes plain and then red again.
  • ColorLookup and HueCorrect: Adjust in Viewer (it was Key from Viewer) now takes a drag. Press on a color in the Viewer and drag up or down to raise or lower the curve at that color; the whole drag is one undo. A click still puts a key there, and a pen's tap counts as a click.
  • In the Node Graph, dragging from an output that already has a wire now picks that wire up, as pressing the ball in an input's socket does. Let go on another node's output and that node feeds what the wire fed; let go on empty ground to disconnect it. When several wires leave the output, the one heading the way you drag comes away. To start a new wire from a wired output, hold Shift as you drag. Picking a wire up by its input end now works from the ball itself too, and dropping it on empty ground disconnects it (to pull a new wire from a wired input to an output, hold Shift). A picked-up end let go on a Dot runs through the Dot. Each is one undo.
  • ReadSplat's came from menu: Postshot, Polycam and KIRI Engine no longer say "not verified yet" for their up axis. Captures from each, shared on SuperSplat, stand upright with Y down, the setting these entries already chose. Their colorspace is still unchecked, and so are Luma AI's (its sample stood up Y down but tipped) and DJI Terra's (no sample yet).
  • ColorCurves spares grays better. A new ColorCurves fades its hue curves toward gray with a steeper shape at 0.06 (the spare grays row's new Steep fade), so the grain on a gray wall or a white car takes far less of a hue turn (about 2 degrees of a 20 degree turn, was about 9, measured on 10 studio plates) while pale colors such as skin in shade still take most of it. ColorCurves nodes in comps saved before open with the Gentle fade they had and look exactly as they did; choose Steep and 0.06 to give one the new fade.
  • The Node Graph stays readable at every interface brightness. Wires, ports and grid dots now lift with the ground, and the small words under the tiles get lighter as the tiles do: at brightness 30 wires are 4.5:1 on the ground (were 3:1) and the words 4.5:1 on every tile (were 3.1:1). Dark looks exactly as before.
  • Going back to a frame you have just looked at is now close to instant on a 16 GB Mac. The Viewer keeps the last frames it showed, in a part of the image cache set aside for them (half the render engine's share, so the total memory is the same). On a heavy 4K studio comp on a 16 GB Mac mini, a frame seen again took 7.6 seconds, as long as a new one; it now takes about 0.7. On a bigger Mac, 1.3 seconds became 0.65.
  • Motion blur on a moving Transform (a match move, for instance) is now added up on the GPU in one pass, with the same pixels as before. On a studio comp whose match move blurs 24 copies of a 4K plate, that part of a frame took 1.7 to 3.7 seconds on a 16 GB Mac mini and now takes about 0.3; a new frame in the Viewer went from 6.9 to 5.1 seconds.
  • The first frame of a comp with a learned model shows sooner. Most of its extra time was spent working out the model's input picture the slow way, a node at a time; that picture now comes from Kento's render engine, and only the channels the model reads. On a studio comp with DepthAnythingV2, the first picture after opening took 18 to 22 seconds on a 16 GB Mac mini and now takes 12 to 14; on a Mac Studio, 10 seconds became 6. Moving to another frame while the model is still running no longer waits for the model to finish.
  • Comps with a learned model (an Inference node, inside gizmos such as DepthAnythingV2) do less work at each new frame. Kento checked whether the model's input picture had changed once for every processor thread, up to 30 times a frame; it now checks once. On a heavy studio comp that is about 20 seconds less processor time a frame spent checking.
  • Furea's lens readout, LensDefocus's kernel preview, Roto's shape outlines and PixelKernel's kernel check no longer pause the rest of the interface while they work.

Fixed

  • A Flipbook made "As the Viewer shows it" with a cache node no longer hands its smaller frames to renders. Those frames are worked out at the Viewer's downscale, and a render through the cache node read them as if they were full size, so the render came out soft. The cache node now keeps the size each frame was made at: the Viewer at that downscale plays them, and a render, or the Viewer at full size, works the picture out at full size instead. Render out of date on the node makes them again at full size. After the comp is closed and opened again, an edit above the cache node still drops the frames it changes.
  • A file rewritten in place within the same second and at the same size (a quick re-render of an uncompressed DPX or EXR) is read again by renders and in the next session. Kento told a file's versions apart by its time to the second; it now uses the time to the nanosecond and the size, for the engine's results in memory and on disk, its file reads, decoded stills, layered files and movies, Edit mode's pictures and the proof sheet's copies. Decoded movies and stills are made once more after updating. A Viewer already showing the file still needs Reload, as before.
  • The Viewer no longer stays at Updating for minutes on a heavy comp. While the Viewer's picture caught up with a pan, a zoom or a window settling, the tiles it hadn't reached yet were worked out the slow way, a node at a time; on a heavy studio comp's car merge one tile took a minute, the Viewer said Updating for ten, and the interface stopped answering meanwhile. Those tiles now come from Kento's render engine too: the picture is there in about two seconds.
  • SmartMerge's Measure no longer stops the interface. It reads the shot in the background: the row says it's reading, with Cancel, and you can go on working; the numbers come in as one undo. Measure the defocus reads in the background too. SmartMerge and Levels read the plate and the element through Kento's render engine, so Measure on a heavy studio comp's car merge takes about 8 seconds for five frames (it froze the app for about ten minutes).
  • SmartMerge's read region follows a drag. The plate and the element are read once, then each change of the read menu, the band's width or the box is worked out in a fraction of a second, so the outline follows the band's square as you drag it. While the plate is read again (another frame, an upstream change) the last outline stays in the Viewer and its chip says it's reading.
  • The pick-whip's dotted line is drawn over Kento's own windows only. Before, it was drawn in a window the size of the screen that stayed above every app, and if a drag hung it stayed up over other apps too. It also goes away by itself once the drag is over.
  • ColorLookup's Adjust in Viewer moves the curve at a gentler pace: a stop for every 100 pixels you drag while the graph is shown in stops, and the curve's whole 0 to 1 over 400 pixels when it is shown 0 to 1 (Option still a tenth of that). Before, a short drag could move a gray to more than twice its value. A key dragged above the curve's last key no longer makes the curve fall below 0 past it, which had put colored streaks in bright highlights.
  • Adjust in Viewer (ColorLookup, HueCorrect) lets go when another node's panel opens above its own. Before, it stayed armed over the other node's picture, and a drag there made an undo step that changed nothing.
  • Clicking a node whose panel isn't open now scrolls the Properties bin to its panel. Before, the panel opened at the top while the bin stayed scrolled down, out of sight.
  • A node's name in the Node Graph stays inside its tile between 45% and 100% zoom: on two lines split where a word starts (Multi and Merge1, Color and Correct1) when one doesn't hold it, or whole under the tile when that doesn't work (Transform1 at about 50%, as further out). Before, MultiMerge1 and other names ran past the tile's end, under its right-hand port, at 50 to 66%.
  • Kento's splash at launch no longer floats over other apps: it shows over Kento only, and hides while you're in another app. Before, during a slow start it sat in the middle of the screen above every app and took clicks meant for them.
  • A ProofSheet's labels are drawn only while the Viewer shows the sheet, not over other nodes' pictures while its panel is open.
  • A wire dropped on a ProofSheet's tile goes to its next free input instead of replacing the first one.
  • Kento's assistant and Kento's other online services can connect again. With a hosted service (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or another https address), Settings' Test said Not reached even with a good key, and the assistant couldn't talk to it; the Hugging Face model list and the Shot panel's upload of a review movie failed the same way. They now connect through the system's own secure connection, and your API key is never shown to other programs on the computer. When a service turns a key down, Test now says Key refused, with the service's reason in its tooltip.
  • Settings' Test for Kento's assistant now says Key refused when a service turns your key down, even if it listed its models for you before. It used to show the old list's count, as if the key worked. The old list is still shown when the service can't be reached at all.
  • Your assistant API key and Kento's seat are no longer visible to other programs on the computer while Kento saves the key in the Mac's keychain or downloads LearnedLens's network or Kiri's MEMatte weights. Before, each was briefly in a system tool's command line, where any program listing the running processes could read it.
  • On the Mac, holding Control before you press on a node and dragging now takes the node out of its chain, as the manual says. Before, the Mac treated the press as a Control-click and opened the node's menu, and only Control pressed after the drag began worked. A Control-click that doesn't move still opens the menu.
  • Starting a wire on a large comp stays quick: whether each input would make a loop is worked out in one pass for the whole drag.
  • A wire that would make a loop now looks refused while you drag it, as a wire of the wrong kind does: the input fades, the loose end turns amber and struck through over it with the reason under the pointer, and letting go there shows a card saying why. Before, the input lit as if it would take the wire and the refusal said nothing. This works for new wires and for wires you pick up.
  • A ProofSheet cell you see alone in the Viewer (or scrub with its time bar) is now only how the Viewer shows it: a Write rendered at the same time, the render queue and a saved comp get the whole sheet. Before, a Write rendered while a cell was soloed rendered that one cell.
  • An AppendClip, ContactSheet or other node whose inputs grow as you wire them no longer prints an error each time it is rewired after its last inputs were disconnected.
  • A node that fails, such as a Read whose file is missing, no longer shows a red warning triangle half hidden behind its tile in the Node Graph, nor on the nodes and Dots below it. The failed node keeps its red edge and mark, a Read says "No picture", and its error card says what went wrong. Zoomed far out, the red edge no longer thins to nothing, so a failed node still shows.
  • A Grade with blackpoint equal to whitepoint now makes a hard step at that point, as Nuke's does. It used to pass the values through without a step. Comps that use this to turn any value above a point into a solid matte (a Grade on alpha with whitepoint 0, say) now look as they do in Nuke, so a Kento comp with such a Grade renders differently from before.
  • SmartMerge's color from a neutral picked in A now reads the place you picked. It read the same spot mirrored top to bottom, so a neutral picked high in A was read low in A.
  • RemoveGlare's glare fitted to a light now matches full size at a Viewer's 1:2 and 1:4 (and in the comp's proxy). At a smaller scale the fit measured the light in the smaller frame's own pixels, so it started and ended in other places and came out flatter: on the 10 studio plates where a light was fitted, the picture at 1:4 was 6.5% off full size on average and up to 20%. It now measures in full-size pixels: at 1:2 the picture matches full size, at 1:4 it is 0.7% off on average (one plate 5.9%, its falloff a step off). At 1:8, where the frame holds less of the light, it is 8% off on average (was 19%, up to 77%).
1.0.14 (build 4832)   Nov 17, 2026

New

  • A calmer Node Graph. Nothing on the graph moves, grows or appears unless you point at it: an input is named while the pointer is on it, and the selected node's wired inputs are named; the rest of the graph stays as it is. A computing node shows a yellow edge once it has worked for 0.4 seconds, and keeps its own color. Glows and flow chevrons are off by default (Settings > Node Graph).
  • One rule for inputs on every node: a node's main inputs always show (B and A on a merge, the first input elsewhere); every other input folds while nothing is wired to it into a small empty socket, with +2, +3 when there are more. Point at the node, or bring a wire near it, and they open in place. MultiMerge's mask inputs keep their own setting for now.
  • Pins and sockets: inputs are sockets and outputs are pins, and a wire ends in a ball seated in its input and starts in a cup round its output's pin, so the flow reads at either end. Pull a wire and its loose end is a ball; within about 28 pixels of an input that takes it, the ball jumps into the socket and the input is named, and letting go lands it exactly there, at any zoom. An input that won't take it leaves the ball outside, amber and struck through.
  • Easier to look at: six node families, each its own color and icon shape, lifted off the ground; brighter wires; long names on two lines instead of cut in the middle, and under the node when zoomed out; the words under nodes only where they can be read (from 75%, or on the selected node). A comp's graph opens with its wires already routed, a failed node keeps its red edge through an edit until it has computed again, and a plate that won't read shows "No picture" on its node.
  • Levels (Color menu): black, gray and white set on a histogram read in stops, so a scene-linear plate's shadows and sun each get room. Drag the histogram's handles or its Blacks, Mid-tones and Whites regions, type the values, or pick each From Viewer. Black and white say what they become (the white can instead keep its brightness, only made neutral). What's below 0, over the top, NaN or infinite is counted and never clamped. Option-drag a handle to see what it clips; Clipping in Viewer stripes it while you work.
  • Levels' Auto sets the ends, the ends and a neutral gray, or each channel's ends, then lists each thing it set and why, every line a switch, with Keep and Undo Auto. Presets by situation, with an amount.
  • Levels' Match to a reference moves A's histogram onto the plate's on input B (the ends, the whole histogram, or the colors too), read in boxes you draw or in A's alpha and the plate near it, and shows the curve it makes. Open as Color Curves puts that curve in a ColorCurves node to keep shaping.
  • ColorCurves (Color menu): every curve in one node, Tone (luma, red, green and blue) and Hue vs Hue, Hue vs Sat, Hue vs Lum, Lum vs Sat, Sat vs Sat and Sat vs Lum, worked out together in log and OKLCh with linear in and out. The picture's own spread sits behind each curve; curves never overshoot their points and hue wraps; values below 0 and above 1 pass through. Spare grays fades the hue curves out toward gray so neutral areas keep their color, and specular highlights keep their hue.
  • ColorCurves in the Viewer: press on a color and drag up or down to move the open curve there, click to add a point, Shift-drag to read an area; Neutral from Viewer, Blacks to..., and named markers shared with the Pixel inspector's pins.
  • ColorCurves' Simple view: situation presets you can preview by hovering, with an amount; shadows, darks, lights and highlights with split marks; eight colors with painted hue, saturation and brightness sliders; an eye on each section for a before and after.
  • The Scopes panel reads in stops as a choice, beside linear and display: every stop the same width, 0.18 and 1.0 marked, out-of-range values counted at the ends.
  • ColorWheels, a new color node: shadows, midtones, highlights and global hue and saturation wheels, each with its own luminance, with blending and balance, painted through the comp's Viewer display. An eye on each range turns it off (hold it to compare); presets with an amount (Split tone: teal and orange, Warm highlights, Cool shadows, Neutralize); Neutral from the Viewer takes a cast out with one click, and Shadows to... and Highlights to... give the picture's shadows or highlights the cast of the plate's, clicked in the Viewer. It grades in a log space, so it suits scene-linear plates, and runs on the GPU. A .nk gets a group with one Expression node doing the same sums.
  • Jump between keys. Two buttons in the transport, either side of the frame steps, and Option+Left and Option+Right go to the previous and next key of the selected nodes, from the Viewer, Timeline, Dope Sheet or Curve Editor. Hover an animated row in Properties and two small arrows beside its key diamond jump between that control's own keys. Both stop playback, never move past the first or last key, and are dim where there is no key that way.
  • View selected: the eye on the Node Graph's toolbar (also in Settings > Node Graph) shows whichever node you select in the Viewer, as pressing 1 would. Turning it on or off isn't an undo step.
  • Touching two nodes links them: drop a node so its tile touches another and the one above feeds the one below, where that input is free (an existing wire is never replaced). Hold Control while dragging to take nodes out of their chain; the chain joins up behind them, and connected nodes dragged together come away as one piece. One undo puts them back in their chain and where they were.
  • Move nodes below to fit (Settings > Node Graph, and the graph's Arrange menu): nodes below move down to make room for a node put in between two, and move up to close the gap a deleted node leaves, unless another node sits level with it.
  • Open and Save windows take a typed or pasted path: click the path bar, press Cmd-L or Shift-Cmd-G, or paste or type a path starting with / or ~. Return opens the folder, or the file; Esc puts the folders back.
  • The Kura Write has a matte task for color-grade mattes. It renders to renders/matte with alpha, as PNG 8-bit written raw (no color transform, so a full matte stays 1 in every channel); 16-bit and EXR (ACEScg) are still available. Comps saved before keep their task.
  • Projection has guided steps: on Simple it shows six steps (Use, Picture, Hold, Surface, Check, Finish), with only the current step's rows showing and All controls one click away. A still with no camera is offered Tour into the picture, in the steps and in Properties' "No camera yet" line; in that mode the steps are the tour's own five, kept with the Viewer's bar.
  • SmartMerge has an Edge section: soften and choke (or grow) A's matte edge before it goes over, so an element doesn't look cut out. Measure compares A's edge with the plate's own edges near A and softens it by the difference. After measuring, SmartMerge checks its own result against the plate beside A and says what's still off, such as an edge still harder than the plate's or too little grain.
  • SmartMerge's preset row has Sit in shade: it lifts A's shadows to the plate's black near A, with no haze, and takes a little of A's saturation. A new saturation control, under Color, does the same by hand.
  • Furea's lens picker: the lens row opens a picker in place of the long lens menu. Each design is drawn in section with a ghost's path; studio lenses are listed by maker, with a zoom shown once with its measured focals; plus imported .lens files, Find, and the focal as chips.
  • Furea bends by the lens's distortion: choose a studio lens and set bend by its distortion (0 to 1, off by default) to curve the flare's ghosts, streak and glow by that lens's measured distortion. Each light's core stays on its light, and comps saved before render as they did.
  • Furea: every element has its own glow, with glow intensity and glow spread rows in its section. The anamorphic's soft cyan bloom round the light is now the Core's glow, the streak's halo and faint band are the Horizontal streak's glow, and any other element can take a soft glow of its own (none until you raise it). Flares and comps you already have render exactly as before.

Improved

  • ColorLookup, HueCorrect and HSVTool show the picture behind their graphs and take picks from the Viewer: ColorLookup is drawn in stops (its own 0 to 1 a click away) with the picture's brightness behind; HueCorrect shows the picture's hues behind a hue strip in degrees; Key from Viewer marks where the pixel under the pointer sits on the curve and keys it with a click; the target eyedropper reads what the Viewer shows. Keys you add take slopes that never overshoot, written so Nuke draws the same curve, and HueCorrect keeps 0 and 6 one value. HSVTool's Source from Viewer sets its ranges round the color you click and Target from Viewer the change to another; its hue range is drawn as a band over the picture's hues. What these nodes write is still what Nuke reads.
  • Viewers check whether they're on screen only when something changes (a tab, a window, a divider dragged, Kento coming forward), plus once a second, instead of four times a second each and on every redraw. That frees Python for the render threads while a comp works out its frames.
  • Painted slider tracks: a color control shows what it does before you touch it. Saturation runs from gray to full color, a hue rotation sweeps the color wheel, a gain dark to light, a channel's gain dark to its color, each with a small mark where it does nothing, on Grade's and ColorCorrect's color rows, HSVTool, HueShift, Saturation, EXPTool and Gamma. The colors, and every color row's swatch, are shown through the comp's Viewer display, so they match the picture whatever the comp's color space.
  • A node added while the upper of two connected nodes is selected goes in between them: in the gap when it fits, else beside the selected node, and only then under the lower one. Before, it often went to the foot of the graph.
  • Routed wires keep their distance from nodes: a wire runs down the middle of the gap between nodes where there's room, rather than along a node's edge, never at the cost of another bend.
  • Calmer wires: a wire into a side input (A, a mask) that sits higher than its output goes down, across, straight up and in, square like every routed wire, when that crosses no node. A top input higher than its output is routed round its node (Straight wires back up, on by default).
  • Dragging a row by its handle to reorder it shows a blue line where it will land, the same everywhere: Furea's elements, MultiMerge layers, the render queue, Render in order, the Properties bin, Favorites, the Paint tools and stroke history, and the toolbar's groups. No line shows where the drop would change nothing.
  • Scrubbing a number field is steadier: a step every 8 pixels (was 4), a wobble up or down no longer jumps the value, and Shift, Option or a move up or down change the step from then on, never what's already dragged. This now holds for every number field, including the few panels that used the older fields.
  • The color picker updates as you change it: a node's color (a Grade's gain, lift and the rest) follows the picker live, so the Viewer shows it before OK. The same goes for a Roto shape's color (in Properties and on the Viewer's bar), Paint's brush and the strokes being edited, the stroke inspector, Furea's tints and element colors, HeatHaze's key and steam colors, and a transition's edge. OK keeps it as one undo step; Cancel puts the color back.
  • Faster Viewer frames in comps with expressions and Python nodes: the Viewer's render no longer waits behind the interface's own work. On a large show comp, setting up a frame went from 20 to 29 seconds to about 3.
  • A Kura Write keeps PNG or EXR picked on the Write's own tab: its Kura file and path follow (PNG 16-bit when the datatype is 16 bit) instead of going back to EXR.
  • SmartMerge's inputs sit as a Merge's do: B on top, A from the left and the mask on the right, with B and A named where their wires arrive. A used to come in on top beside B, so its wire ran under the tile.
  • A Projection no longer fills the Node Graph with nodes you didn't ask for: Tour into the picture's cameras and room, a plane drawn on the plate, a camera made from it and the grain-free hold all live inside the Projection. Break out (on the plane's line, the hold row, and in the tour's For 3D work) puts them in the comp as nodes wired to it when you want them, as one undo; Camera out puts the move's camera out. Comps saved with those nodes outside keep them and render the same.
  • Furea's output says what it does: Over the plate, Screened over the plate or Flare alone, each with a few words beside it. A new Furea always comes up over the plate; a kept flare no longer carries Flare alone onto it.
  • Furea's element layer row reads "into layer", names the element's own layer, says it picks the channels the element is written to with Separate layers, and is dim while the flare is one layer.
  • Furea's looks can be tried freely: each element's look menu starts with Original (the values it arrived with, saying where from), which a look never overwrites, and your own edits come back as Your changes after you try another look.
  • Furea's Ghosts from: keep a studio lens and take its ghosts from any of Kento's designs. Choosing a design or Automatic now clears the studio lens, so the row never names a lens it isn't using.
  • Furea's streak side is now bias: even in the middle of its slider, left and right at each end.
  • Furea's start from menu shows each flare as an icon built from its own elements, layered in their colors and strengths, with the light's color, a spike for each blade and the ghosts where the lens puts them, so the starters no longer look alike. Your flares and the studio's get theirs too, and the closed menu shows the flare as it is now.

Fixed

  • Help > Release notes names the version you're running; 1.0.13's said Beta 1.0.12.
  • A plate that won't read no longer makes its node flash in the Node Graph about once a second: its thumbnail is tried again when the node or the frame changes, not every second.
  • Pointing at an input in the Node Graph no longer draws the white ring that means a wire would land there. The ring shows only while you drag a wire.
  • Zoomed far out in the Node Graph, dragging a small node by the edge near its output only moves it. Let go over another node, it was sometimes also wired into that node, even into two of its inputs.
  • Furea, RemoveGlare, LensDefocus, LensWarp, ChromaticAberration, MapDefocus, EdgeWrap (SmartMerge's edge wrap too), PickMatte, Lens, MatteRefine and Kiri look as they do at 1:1 when the Viewer works at 1:2 or smaller (and in the comp's proxy), as far as the smaller frame can hold their detail. A Furea light, RemoveGlare source or PickMatte point on the right half of the plate fell off the smaller frame, so nothing flared, nothing was taken out or no matte grew; LensWarp's warp sat off its center; ChromaticAberration's fringes turned about the wrong point; an off-center Lens moved its center twice as far; the defocus blurs, MatteRefine's band and RemoveGlare's spread, band and streak sizes doubled; the edge wrap and Kiri's background blurs shrank to a quarter. RemoveGlare's glare fitted to the light still differs at 1:4 and smaller. PlateAlign was checked and already matched.
  • A comp holding a clone of a node imported from a Nuke script can be saved again; the save was refused, saying the clones would be left out of the file. A clone is now saved as a clone with its own name, and opens still linked to its original.
  • A knob linked straight to another node's knob is kept when the comp is saved. It came back from the .ko as a copied value, no longer following the other knob. It now reopens linked, a whole knob or one part of one, and an exported .nk writes it as the link expression, such as {{Grade1.black}}.
  • Roto and RotoPaint layers, shapes and strokes linked by expression to another node (a layer riding a match move's Transform, or a shape offset from it) now follow it, as the script intended: an imported car roto that came in about 350 pixels off now sits on the car. The link is live: key or track the Transform again in Kento and the shapes move with it, motion blur included. The expressions are saved as written, in a .ko and an exported .nk. A link to a node that isn't in the comp reads 0, and the import's notice names it.
  • A Roto's feather, source and brush type as Nuke's panel last showed them, and a planar track's corners, are kept and saved back.
  • A render that was running when Kento closed no longer starts again by itself with the next session's first render. It opens paused in the Render Queue, its row saying it stopped when Kento closed, until you choose Resume. A finished job never renders again on its own.
  • A Viewer on a Write in a big comp shows its picture and plays: it could show nothing after 40 seconds and never leave the first frame. It now takes about 5 seconds, the same picture.
  • Frame steps and playback no longer freeze for several seconds when the cache folder is on a network share: a large comp went from 16 seconds a frame, with freezes of up to 8 seconds, to under 4 seconds a frame without freezing. On a network share, Keep slow render results here for later sessions (Settings, Performance) stays off and says why.
  • A big comp no longer stalls while the Optimize tab works out what it costs. Optimize now measures only when you press Measure: at the current frame, inside the frame range, as a render does, behind the Viewer on half the processor cores, and it stops when you change frames or start a render.
  • Reading a pixel through Kento's remote control no longer stops the interface: it's read in the background, as a frame render is.
  • Keying a position, a color or any control with several parts keys every part. Furea's light dragged in the Viewer on a new frame keyed only its x; the key diamond on a row of x and y fields keyed only x. Now the diamond, the Viewer's handles, the color rows, the eyedropper and Pick in Viewer key all the parts at once.
  • Furea's light menu lists all five lights; it offered only the current one.
  • Furea's Add element button opens its list of elements again; the menu closed before it showed.
  • HeatHaze: moving a slider while the air is simulated is never interrupted. The steps no longer jump back to Play or turn Next off while it works; "Simulating" shows on the status line under the panel, with its running bar, so no row moves under the pointer.
  • HeatHaze: the Viewer's pointer follows the tool. Drawing a point, line or shape shows a crosshair, and the depth and key picks show the eyedropper. A pick lets go when the step changes, and the HeatHaze row over the Viewer lights whichever tool is on.
  • HeatHaze: emitters drawn in the Simple steps show in the Viewer, with handles you can drag, at every step and when the steps are folded (they showed in All controls only); a line's first end shows as soon as you click it.

  • Opening a comp no longer pins SmartMerge's settings as if you had set them by hand, so Automatic keeps following the shot after a comp is reopened.
  • A Tour into the picture with a thing in it, saved and opened again, rendered nothing where the room should be. The room is made again when the comp opens.

  • In Tour into the picture's Move step, the room's lines and the things' outlines follow the moving picture. The room's handles and size labels show on the still only.

New: Tour into the picture

  • One still becomes a room the camera moves through. Projection has a new mode for a single picture, Tour into the picture: right-click a still in the Viewer and choose Tour into this picture, or add a Projection to a still. Five steps, shown on the Viewer's bar and free to jump between: Picture, Room, Things, Fill and Move. Next always names the next thing to do.
  • Room: the room is found from the picture's own straight edges, as the Perspective node finds lines, and drawn over the still at once as a first guess you correct. Drag where the lines meet, a corner of the back wall, or a line's end onto an edge in the picture. A solved Perspective node up the still can seed the room and its lens instead. Click two points and type how long they are to give the room a real size, in meters or feet.
  • Things: click round a thing and it stands where its foot touches, on the floor, hanging from the ceiling or out of a wall. Drag its foot nearer or farther and its top for its height, stand one thing on another, or make one from a Roto shape or a node's alpha.
  • Fill: what the still never showed (behind each thing, and past the picture's edges) is hatched and filled from the pixels around it, so a move that drifts past the edge sees picture, not black. When the room or a thing moves afterward, Fill says it is out of date and offers Fill again.
  • Move: presets named by situation, sliders for push in, drift, rise, turn, tilt, orbit and lens, a map of the room from above, and flying in the Viewer. When the move would see what the picture never showed, a card says where and offers Fill it or Limit the move. Out gives the moving picture at the comp's format; for 3D work, the camera, the room's lines as a Perspective node, and the room and its things as USD or Alembic. In a Nuke script it's offered for baking, with Nuke cameras.

  • Kento's more involved tools now open on a few short steps instead of every control at once. A strip at the top of the panel shows where you are; each step says in one line what to do and shows only its own controls, and Next names the step it goes to. When a step can't go on, an amber line says why with the one button that fixes it ("Couldn't measure: A has too little solid matte", Measure again), and the Viewer's top left shows the same words.
