For a calmer graph, Settings > Node Graph > Fold Wired Inputs folds a busy node's wired extra inputs into that socket too. When the pointer leaves, they stay open for a moment so you can follow a wire, then fold back (Settings > Node Graph > Inputs Stay Open, 1.2 seconds). To keep a node's inputs open all the time, turn on keep inputs open in its Node tab, or select it and press Shift+H (Edit > Keep Inputs Open); the comp remembers it. A merge's operation (over, min) is now inside the tile with its name. Resting the pointer on an input says what it is for and where it comes from ("A2: laid over B with min", "From Grade3"), instead of an internal name, and a node's tooltip lists where its inputs come from.
  • The Node Graph's Viewer and MultiMerge follow the same inputs rule as every other node. A Viewer's input 1 always shows, its wired inputs show, and its other free inputs fold into one small socket with their count (+9 on a new Viewer); a wire dropped anywhere on an empty Viewer still goes to input 1. A MultiMerge's background and first layer always show, and a layer's mask input folds until it is wired.
  • Zooming the Node Graph no longer pops details in and out: names, icons, the words under tiles and the dots on wired ports fade over a few percent of zoom.
  • A failed node's red edge now stays while the node is still computing after an edit, however long that takes, so a slow node no longer flashes plain and then red again.
  • ColorLookup and HueCorrect: Adjust in Viewer (it was Key from Viewer) now takes a drag. Press on a color in the Viewer and drag up or down to raise or lower the curve at that color; the whole drag is one undo. A click still puts a key there, and a pen's tap counts as a click.
  • In the Node Graph, dragging from an output that already has a wire now picks that wire up, as pressing the ball in an input's socket does. Let go on another node's output and that node feeds what the wire fed; let go on empty ground to disconnect it. When several wires leave the output, the one heading the way you drag comes away. To start a new wire from a wired output, hold Shift as you drag. Picking a wire up by its input end now works from the ball itself too, and dropping it on empty ground disconnects it (to pull a new wire from a wired input to an output, hold Shift). A picked-up end let go on a Dot runs through the Dot. Each is one undo.
  • ReadSplat's came from menu: Postshot, Polycam and KIRI Engine no longer say "not verified yet" for their up axis. Captures from each, shared on SuperSplat, stand upright with Y down, the setting these entries already chose. Their colorspace is still unchecked, and so are Luma AI's (its sample stood up Y down but tipped) and DJI Terra's (no sample yet).
  • ColorCurves spares grays better. A new ColorCurves fades its hue curves toward gray with a steeper shape at 0.06 (the spare grays row's new Steep fade), so the grain on a gray wall or a white car takes far less of a hue turn (about 2 degrees of a 20 degree turn, was about 9, measured on 10 studio plates) while pale colors such as skin in shade still take most of it. ColorCurves nodes in comps saved before open with the Gentle fade they had and look exactly as they did; choose Steep and 0.06 to give one the new fade.
  • The Node Graph stays readable at every interface brightness. Wires, ports and grid dots now lift with the ground, and the small words under the tiles get lighter as the tiles do: at brightness 30 wires are 4.5:1 on the ground (were 3:1) and the words 4.5:1 on every tile (were 3.1:1). Dark looks exactly as before.
  • Going back to a frame you have just looked at is now close to instant on a 16 GB Mac. The Viewer keeps the last frames it showed, in a part of the image cache set aside for them (half the render engine's share, so the total memory is the same). On a heavy 4K studio comp on a 16 GB Mac mini, a frame seen again took 7.6 seconds, as long as a new one; it now takes about 0.7. On a bigger Mac, 1.3 seconds became 0.65.
  • Motion blur on a moving Transform (a match move, for instance) is now added up on the GPU in one pass, with the same pixels as before. On a studio comp whose match move blurs 24 copies of a 4K plate, that part of a frame took 1.7 to 3.7 seconds on a 16 GB Mac mini and now takes about 0.3; a new frame in the Viewer went from 6.9 to 5.1 seconds.
  • The first frame of a comp with a learned model shows sooner. Most of its extra time was spent working out the model's input picture the slow way, a node at a time; that picture now comes from Kento's render engine, and only the channels the model reads. On a studio comp with DepthAnythingV2, the first picture after opening took 18 to 22 seconds on a 16 GB Mac mini and now takes 12 to 14; on a Mac Studio, 10 seconds became 6. Moving to another frame while the model is still running no longer waits for the model to finish.
  • Comps with a learned model (an Inference node, inside gizmos such as DepthAnythingV2) do less work at each new frame. Kento checked whether the model's input picture had changed once for every processor thread, up to 30 times a frame; it now checks once. On a heavy studio comp that is about 20 seconds less processor time a frame spent checking.
  • Furea's lens readout, LensDefocus's kernel preview, Roto's shape outlines and PixelKernel's kernel check no longer pause the rest of the interface while they work.

Fixed

  • A Flipbook made "As the Viewer shows it" with a cache node no longer hands its smaller frames to renders. Those frames are worked out at the Viewer's downscale, and a render through the cache node read them as if they were full size, so the render came out soft. The cache node now keeps the size each frame was made at: the Viewer at that downscale plays them, and a render, or the Viewer at full size, works the picture out at full size instead. Render out of date on the node makes them again at full size. After the comp is closed and opened again, an edit above the cache node still drops the frames it changes.
  • A file rewritten in place within the same second and at the same size (a quick re-render of an uncompressed DPX or EXR) is read again by renders and in the next session. Kento told a file's versions apart by its time to the second; it now uses the time to the nanosecond and the size, for the engine's results in memory and on disk, its file reads, decoded stills, layered files and movies, Edit mode's pictures and the proof sheet's copies. Decoded movies and stills are made once more after updating. A Viewer already showing the file still needs Reload, as before.
  • The Viewer no longer stays at Updating for minutes on a heavy comp. While the Viewer's picture caught up with a pan, a zoom or a window settling, the tiles it hadn't reached yet were worked out the slow way, a node at a time; on a heavy studio comp's car merge one tile took a minute, the Viewer said Updating for ten, and the interface stopped answering meanwhile. Those tiles now come from Kento's render engine too: the picture is there in about two seconds.
  • SmartMerge's Measure no longer stops the interface. It reads the shot in the background: the row says it's reading, with Cancel, and you can go on working; the numbers come in as one undo. Measure the defocus reads in the background too. SmartMerge and Levels read the plate and the element through Kento's render engine, so Measure on a heavy studio comp's car merge takes about 8 seconds for five frames (it froze the app for about ten minutes).
  • SmartMerge's read region follows a drag. The plate and the element are read once, then each change of the read menu, the band's width or the box is worked out in a fraction of a second, so the outline follows the band's square as you drag it. While the plate is read again (another frame, an upstream change) the last outline stays in the Viewer and its chip says it's reading.
  • The pick-whip's dotted line is drawn over Kento's own windows only. Before, it was drawn in a window the size of the screen that stayed above every app, and if a drag hung it stayed up over other apps too. It also goes away by itself once the drag is over.
  • ColorLookup's Adjust in Viewer moves the curve at a gentler pace: a stop for every 100 pixels you drag while the graph is shown in stops, and the curve's whole 0 to 1 over 400 pixels when it is shown 0 to 1 (Option still a tenth of that). Before, a short drag could move a gray to more than twice its value. A key dragged above the curve's last key no longer makes the curve fall below 0 past it, which had put colored streaks in bright highlights.
  • Adjust in Viewer (ColorLookup, HueCorrect) lets go when another node's panel opens above its own. Before, it stayed armed over the other node's picture, and a drag there made an undo step that changed nothing.
  • Clicking a node whose panel isn't open now scrolls the Properties bin to its panel. Before, the panel opened at the top while the bin stayed scrolled down, out of sight.
  • A node's name in the Node Graph stays inside its tile between 45% and 100% zoom: on two lines split where a word starts (Multi and Merge1, Color and Correct1) when one doesn't hold it, or whole under the tile when that doesn't work (Transform1 at about 50%, as further out). Before, MultiMerge1 and other names ran past the tile's end, under its right-hand port, at 50 to 66%.
  • Kento's splash at launch no longer floats over other apps: it shows over Kento only, and hides while you're in another app. Before, during a slow start it sat in the middle of the screen above every app and took clicks meant for them.
  • A ProofSheet's labels are drawn only while the Viewer shows the sheet, not over other nodes' pictures while its panel is open.
  • A wire dropped on a ProofSheet's tile goes to its next free input instead of replacing the first one.
  • Kento's assistant and Kento's other online services can connect again. With a hosted service (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or another https address), Settings' Test said Not reached even with a good key, and the assistant couldn't talk to it; the Hugging Face model list and the Shot panel's upload of a review movie failed the same way. They now connect through the system's own secure connection, and your API key is never shown to other programs on the computer. When a service turns a key down, Test now says Key refused, with the service's reason in its tooltip.
  • Settings' Test for Kento's assistant now says Key refused when a service turns your key down, even if it listed its models for you before. It used to show the old list's count, as if the key worked. The old list is still shown when the service can't be reached at all.
  • Your assistant API key and Kento's seat are no longer visible to other programs on the computer while Kento saves the key in the Mac's keychain or downloads LearnedLens's network or Kiri's MEMatte weights. Before, each was briefly in a system tool's command line, where any program listing the running processes could read it.
  • On the Mac, holding Control before you press on a node and dragging now takes the node out of its chain, as the manual says. Before, the Mac treated the press as a Control-click and opened the node's menu, and only Control pressed after the drag began worked. A Control-click that doesn't move still opens the menu.
  • Starting a wire on a large comp stays quick: whether each input would make a loop is worked out in one pass for the whole drag.
  • A wire that would make a loop now looks refused while you drag it, as a wire of the wrong kind does: the input fades, the loose end turns amber and struck through over it with the reason under the pointer, and letting go there shows a card saying why. Before, the input lit as if it would take the wire and the refusal said nothing. This works for new wires and for wires you pick up.
  • A ProofSheet cell you see alone in the Viewer (or scrub with its time bar) is now only how the Viewer shows it: a Write rendered at the same time, the render queue and a saved comp get the whole sheet. Before, a Write rendered while a cell was soloed rendered that one cell.
  • An AppendClip, ContactSheet or other node whose inputs grow as you wire them no longer prints an error each time it is rewired after its last inputs were disconnected.
  • A node that fails, such as a Read whose file is missing, no longer shows a red warning triangle half hidden behind its tile in the Node Graph, nor on the nodes and Dots below it. The failed node keeps its red edge and mark, a Read says "No picture", and its error card says what went wrong. Zoomed far out, the red edge no longer thins to nothing, so a failed node still shows.
  • A Grade with blackpoint equal to whitepoint now makes a hard step at that point, as Nuke's does. It used to pass the values through without a step. Comps that use this to turn any value above a point into a solid matte (a Grade on alpha with whitepoint 0, say) now look as they do in Nuke, so a Kento comp with such a Grade renders differently from before.
  • SmartMerge's color from a neutral picked in A now reads the place you picked. It read the same spot mirrored top to bottom, so a neutral picked high in A was read low in A.
  • RemoveGlare's glare fitted to a light now matches full size at a Viewer's 1:2 and 1:4 (and in the comp's proxy). At a smaller scale the fit measured the light in the smaller frame's own pixels, so it started and ended in other places and came out flatter: on the 10 studio plates where a light was fitted, the picture at 1:4 was 6.5% off full size on average and up to 20%. It now measures in full-size pixels: at 1:2 the picture matches full size, at 1:4 it is 0.7% off on average (one plate 5.9%, its falloff a step off). At 1:8, where the frame holds less of the light, it is 8% off on average (was 19%, up to 77%).
1.0.14 (build 4832)   Nov 17, 2026

New

  • A calmer Node Graph. Nothing on the graph moves, grows or appears unless you point at it: an input is named while the pointer is on it, and the selected node's wired inputs are named; the rest of the graph stays as it is. A computing node shows a yellow edge once it has worked for 0.4 seconds, and keeps its own color. Glows and flow chevrons are off by default (Settings > Node Graph).
  • One rule for inputs on every node: a node's main inputs always show (B and A on a merge, the first input elsewhere); every other input folds while nothing is wired to it into a small empty socket, with +2, +3 when there are more. Point at the node, or bring a wire near it, and they open in place. MultiMerge's mask inputs keep their own setting for now.
  • Pins and sockets: inputs are sockets and outputs are pins, and a wire ends in a ball seated in its input and starts in a cup round its output's pin, so the flow reads at either end. Pull a wire and its loose end is a ball; within about 28 pixels of an input that takes it, the ball jumps into the socket and the input is named, and letting go lands it exactly there, at any zoom. An input that won't take it leaves the ball outside, amber and struck through.
  • Easier to look at: six node families, each its own color and icon shape, lifted off the ground; brighter wires; long names on two lines instead of cut in the middle, and under the node when zoomed out; the words under nodes only where they can be read (from 75%, or on the selected node). A comp's graph opens with its wires already routed, a failed node keeps its red edge through an edit until it has computed again, and a plate that won't read shows "No picture" on its node.
  • Levels (Color menu): black, gray and white set on a histogram read in stops, so a scene-linear plate's shadows and sun each get room. Drag the histogram's handles or its Blacks, Mid-tones and Whites regions, type the values, or pick each From Viewer. Black and white say what they become (the white can instead keep its brightness, only made neutral). What's below 0, over the top, NaN or infinite is counted and never clamped. Option-drag a handle to see what it clips; Clipping in Viewer stripes it while you work.
  • Levels' Auto sets the ends, the ends and a neutral gray, or each channel's ends, then lists each thing it set and why, every line a switch, with Keep and Undo Auto. Presets by situation, with an amount.
  • Levels' Match to a reference moves A's histogram onto the plate's on input B (the ends, the whole histogram, or the colors too), read in boxes you draw or in A's alpha and the plate near it, and shows the curve it makes. Open as Color Curves puts that curve in a ColorCurves node to keep shaping.
  • ColorCurves (Color menu): every curve in one node, Tone (luma, red, green and blue) and Hue vs Hue, Hue vs Sat, Hue vs Lum, Lum vs Sat, Sat vs Sat and Sat vs Lum, worked out together in log and OKLCh with linear in and out. The picture's own spread sits behind each curve; curves never overshoot their points and hue wraps; values below 0 and above 1 pass through. Spare grays fades the hue curves out toward gray so neutral areas keep their color, and specular highlights keep their hue.
  • ColorCurves in the Viewer: press on a color and drag up or down to move the open curve there, click to add a point, Shift-drag to read an area; Neutral from Viewer, Blacks to..., and named markers shared with the Pixel inspector's pins.
  • ColorCurves' Simple view: situation presets you can preview by hovering, with an amount; shadows, darks, lights and highlights with split marks; eight colors with painted hue, saturation and brightness sliders; an eye on each section for a before and after.
  • The Scopes panel reads in stops as a choice, beside linear and display: every stop the same width, 0.18 and 1.0 marked, out-of-range values counted at the ends.
  • ColorWheels, a new color node: shadows, midtones, highlights and global hue and saturation wheels, each with its own luminance, with blending and balance, painted through the comp's Viewer display. An eye on each range turns it off (hold it to compare); presets with an amount (Split tone: teal and orange, Warm highlights, Cool shadows, Neutralize); Neutral from the Viewer takes a cast out with one click, and Shadows to... and Highlights to... give the picture's shadows or highlights the cast of the plate's, clicked in the Viewer. It grades in a log space, so it suits scene-linear plates, and runs on the GPU. A .nk gets a group with one Expression node doing the same sums.
  • Jump between keys. Two buttons in the transport, either side of the frame steps, and Option+Left and Option+Right go to the previous and next key of the selected nodes, from the Viewer, Timeline, Dope Sheet or Curve Editor. Hover an animated row in Properties and two small arrows beside its key diamond jump between that control's own keys. Both stop playback, never move past the first or last key, and are dim where there is no key that way.
  • View selected: the eye on the Node Graph's toolbar (also in Settings > Node Graph) shows whichever node you select in the Viewer, as pressing 1 would. Turning it on or off isn't an undo step.
  • Touching two nodes links them: drop a node so its tile touches another and the one above feeds the one below, where that input is free (an existing wire is never replaced). Hold Control while dragging to take nodes out of their chain; the chain joins up behind them, and connected nodes dragged together come away as one piece. One undo puts them back in their chain and where they were.
  • Move nodes below to fit (Settings > Node Graph, and the graph's Arrange menu): nodes below move down to make room for a node put in between two, and move up to close the gap a deleted node leaves, unless another node sits level with it.
  • Open and Save windows take a typed or pasted path: click the path bar, press Cmd-L or Shift-Cmd-G, or paste or type a path starting with / or ~. Return opens the folder, or the file; Esc puts the folders back.
  • The Kura Write has a matte task for color-grade mattes. It renders to renders/matte with alpha, as PNG 8-bit written raw (no color transform, so a full matte stays 1 in every channel); 16-bit and EXR (ACEScg) are still available. Comps saved before keep their task.
  • Projection has guided steps: on Simple it shows six steps (Use, Picture, Hold, Surface, Check, Finish), with only the current step's rows showing and All controls one click away. A still with no camera is offered Tour into the picture, in the steps and in Properties' "No camera yet" line; in that mode the steps are the tour's own five, kept with the Viewer's bar.
  • SmartMerge has an Edge section: soften and choke (or grow) A's matte edge before it goes over, so an element doesn't look cut out. Measure compares A's edge with the plate's own edges near A and softens it by the difference. After measuring, SmartMerge checks its own result against the plate beside A and says what's still off, such as an edge still harder than the plate's or too little grain.
  • SmartMerge's preset row has Sit in shade: it lifts A's shadows to the plate's black near A, with no haze, and takes a little of A's saturation. A new saturation control, under Color, does the same by hand.
  • Furea's lens picker: the lens row opens a picker in place of the long lens menu. Each design is drawn in section with a ghost's path; studio lenses are listed by maker, with a zoom shown once with its measured focals; plus imported .lens files, Find, and the focal as chips.
  • Furea bends by the lens's distortion: choose a studio lens and set bend by its distortion (0 to 1, off by default) to curve the flare's ghosts, streak and glow by that lens's measured distortion. Each light's core stays on its light, and comps saved before render as they did.
  • Furea: every element has its own glow, with glow intensity and glow spread rows in its section. The anamorphic's soft cyan bloom round the light is now the Core's glow, the streak's halo and faint band are the Horizontal streak's glow, and any other element can take a soft glow of its own (none until you raise it). Flares and comps you already have render exactly as before.

Improved

  • ColorLookup, HueCorrect and HSVTool show the picture behind their graphs and take picks from the Viewer: ColorLookup is drawn in stops (its own 0 to 1 a click away) with the picture's brightness behind; HueCorrect shows the picture's hues behind a hue strip in degrees; Key from Viewer marks where the pixel under the pointer sits on the curve and keys it with a click; the target eyedropper reads what the Viewer shows. Keys you add take slopes that never overshoot, written so Nuke draws the same curve, and HueCorrect keeps 0 and 6 one value. HSVTool's Source from Viewer sets its ranges round the color you click and Target from Viewer the change to another; its hue range is drawn as a band over the picture's hues. What these nodes write is still what Nuke reads.
  • Viewers check whether they're on screen only when something changes (a tab, a window, a divider dragged, Kento coming forward), plus once a second, instead of four times a second each and on every redraw. That frees Python for the render threads while a comp works out its frames.
  • Painted slider tracks: a color control shows what it does before you touch it. Saturation runs from gray to full color, a hue rotation sweeps the color wheel, a gain dark to light, a channel's gain dark to its color, each with a small mark where it does nothing, on Grade's and ColorCorrect's color rows, HSVTool, HueShift, Saturation, EXPTool and Gamma. The colors, and every color row's swatch, are shown through the comp's Viewer display, so they match the picture whatever the comp's color space.
  • A node added while the upper of two connected nodes is selected goes in between them: in the gap when it fits, else beside the selected node, and only then under the lower one. Before, it often went to the foot of the graph.
  • Routed wires keep their distance from nodes: a wire runs down the middle of the gap between nodes where there's room, rather than along a node's edge, never at the cost of another bend.
  • Calmer wires: a wire into a side input (A, a mask) that sits higher than its output goes down, across, straight up and in, square like every routed wire, when that crosses no node. A top input higher than its output is routed round its node (Straight wires back up, on by default).
  • Dragging a row by its handle to reorder it shows a blue line where it will land, the same everywhere: Furea's elements, MultiMerge layers, the render queue, Render in order, the Properties bin, Favorites, the Paint tools and stroke history, and the toolbar's groups. No line shows where the drop would change nothing.
  • Scrubbing a number field is steadier: a step every 8 pixels (was 4), a wobble up or down no longer jumps the value, and Shift, Option or a move up or down change the step from then on, never what's already dragged. This now holds for every number field, including the few panels that used the older fields.
  • The color picker updates as you change it: a node's color (a Grade's gain, lift and the rest) follows the picker live, so the Viewer shows it before OK. The same goes for a Roto shape's color (in Properties and on the Viewer's bar), Paint's brush and the strokes being edited, the stroke inspector, Furea's tints and element colors, HeatHaze's key and steam colors, and a transition's edge. OK keeps it as one undo step; Cancel puts the color back.
  • Faster Viewer frames in comps with expressions and Python nodes: the Viewer's render no longer waits behind the interface's own work. On a large show comp, setting up a frame went from 20 to 29 seconds to about 3.
  • A Kura Write keeps PNG or EXR picked on the Write's own tab: its Kura file and path follow (PNG 16-bit when the datatype is 16 bit) instead of going back to EXR.
  • SmartMerge's inputs sit as a Merge's do: B on top, A from the left and the mask on the right, with B and A named where their wires arrive. A used to come in on top beside B, so its wire ran under the tile.
  • A Projection no longer fills the Node Graph with nodes you didn't ask for: Tour into the picture's cameras and room, a plane drawn on the plate, a camera made from it and the grain-free hold all live inside the Projection. Break out (on the plane's line, the hold row, and in the tour's For 3D work) puts them in the comp as nodes wired to it when you want them, as one undo; Camera out puts the move's camera out. Comps saved with those nodes outside keep them and render the same.
  • Furea's output says what it does: Over the plate, Screened over the plate or Flare alone, each with a few words beside it. A new Furea always comes up over the plate; a kept flare no longer carries Flare alone onto it.
  • Furea's element layer row reads "into layer", names the element's own layer, says it picks the channels the element is written to with Separate layers, and is dim while the flare is one layer.
  • Furea's looks can be tried freely: each element's look menu starts with Original (the values it arrived with, saying where from), which a look never overwrites, and your own edits come back as Your changes after you try another look.
  • Furea's Ghosts from: keep a studio lens and take its ghosts from any of Kento's designs. Choosing a design or Automatic now clears the studio lens, so the row never names a lens it isn't using.
  • Furea's streak side is now bias: even in the middle of its slider, left and right at each end.
  • Furea's start from menu shows each flare as an icon built from its own elements, layered in their colors and strengths, with the light's color, a spike for each blade and the ghosts where the lens puts them, so the starters no longer look alike. Your flares and the studio's get theirs too, and the closed menu shows the flare as it is now.

Fixed

  • Help > Release notes names the version you're running; 1.0.13's said Beta 1.0.12.
  • A plate that won't read no longer makes its node flash in the Node Graph about once a second: its thumbnail is tried again when the node or the frame changes, not every second.
  • Pointing at an input in the Node Graph no longer draws the white ring that means a wire would land there. The ring shows only while you drag a wire.
  • Zoomed far out in the Node Graph, dragging a small node by the edge near its output only moves it. Let go over another node, it was sometimes also wired into that node, even into two of its inputs.
  • Furea, RemoveGlare, LensDefocus, LensWarp, ChromaticAberration, MapDefocus, EdgeWrap (SmartMerge's edge wrap too), PickMatte, Lens, MatteRefine and Kiri look as they do at 1:1 when the Viewer works at 1:2 or smaller (and in the comp's proxy), as far as the smaller frame can hold their detail. A Furea light, RemoveGlare source or PickMatte point on the right half of the plate fell off the smaller frame, so nothing flared, nothing was taken out or no matte grew; LensWarp's warp sat off its center; ChromaticAberration's fringes turned about the wrong point; an off-center Lens moved its center twice as far; the defocus blurs, MatteRefine's band and RemoveGlare's spread, band and streak sizes doubled; the edge wrap and Kiri's background blurs shrank to a quarter. RemoveGlare's glare fitted to the light still differs at 1:4 and smaller. PlateAlign was checked and already matched.
  • A comp holding a clone of a node imported from a Nuke script can be saved again; the save was refused, saying the clones would be left out of the file. A clone is now saved as a clone with its own name, and opens still linked to its original.
  • A knob linked straight to another node's knob is kept when the comp is saved. It came back from the .ko as a copied value, no longer following the other knob. It now reopens linked, a whole knob or one part of one, and an exported .nk writes it as the link expression, such as {{Grade1.black}}.
  • Roto and RotoPaint layers, shapes and strokes linked by expression to another node (a layer riding a match move's Transform, or a shape offset from it) now follow it, as the script intended: an imported car roto that came in about 350 pixels off now sits on the car. The link is live: key or track the Transform again in Kento and the shapes move with it, motion blur included. The expressions are saved as written, in a .ko and an exported .nk. A link to a node that isn't in the comp reads 0, and the import's notice names it.
  • A Roto's feather, source and brush type as Nuke's panel last showed them, and a planar track's corners, are kept and saved back.
  • A render that was running when Kento closed no longer starts again by itself with the next session's first render. It opens paused in the Render Queue, its row saying it stopped when Kento closed, until you choose Resume. A finished job never renders again on its own.
  • A Viewer on a Write in a big comp shows its picture and plays: it could show nothing after 40 seconds and never leave the first frame. It now takes about 5 seconds, the same picture.
  • Frame steps and playback no longer freeze for several seconds when the cache folder is on a network share: a large comp went from 16 seconds a frame, with freezes of up to 8 seconds, to under 4 seconds a frame without freezing. On a network share, Keep slow render results here for later sessions (Settings, Performance) stays off and says why.
  • A big comp no longer stalls while the Optimize tab works out what it costs. Optimize now measures only when you press Measure: at the current frame, inside the frame range, as a render does, behind the Viewer on half the processor cores, and it stops when you change frames or start a render.
  • Reading a pixel through Kento's remote control no longer stops the interface: it's read in the background, as a frame render is.
  • Keying a position, a color or any control with several parts keys every part. Furea's light dragged in the Viewer on a new frame keyed only its x; the key diamond on a row of x and y fields keyed only x. Now the diamond, the Viewer's handles, the color rows, the eyedropper and Pick in Viewer key all the parts at once.
  • Furea's light menu lists all five lights; it offered only the current one.
  • Furea's Add element button opens its list of elements again; the menu closed before it showed.
  • HeatHaze: moving a slider while the air is simulated is never interrupted. The steps no longer jump back to Play or turn Next off while it works; "Simulating" shows on the status line under the panel, with its running bar, so no row moves under the pointer.
  • HeatHaze: the Viewer's pointer follows the tool. Drawing a point, line or shape shows a crosshair, and the depth and key picks show the eyedropper. A pick lets go when the step changes, and the HeatHaze row over the Viewer lights whichever tool is on.
  • HeatHaze: emitters drawn in the Simple steps show in the Viewer, with handles you can drag, at every step and when the steps are folded (they showed in All controls only); a line's first end shows as soon as you click it.
  • HeatHaze at a Viewer's 1:2 to 1:16 (and the comp's proxy) looks as it does at 1:1. Before, an emitter on the right half of the plate fell off the smaller frame and the bend doubled.
  • SmartMerge's color no longer reads the plate's foliage or sky as its balance. It reads the least colorful pixels on each side, and leaves Color off, saying why, when the plate near A has nothing near neutral.
  • SmartMerge's defocus is read at full size along A's edge, not on a small copy where a blur of a few pixels was lost.
  • Opening a comp no longer pins SmartMerge's settings as if you had set them by hand, so Automatic keeps following the shot after a comp is reopened.
  • A Tour into the picture with a thing in it, saved and opened again, rendered nothing where the room should be. The room is made again when the comp opens.
  • Dragging in Projection's Viewer tools no longer stutters after the first drag: the checks after a drag take under a second on a still, and the next drag draws smoothly.
  • In Tour into the picture's Move step, the room's lines and the things' outlines follow the moving picture. The room's handles and size labels show on the still only.
  • The Projection's panel is no longer cut off at the bottom in a narrow Properties panel: a panel whose lines wrap now fits all its rows, the render row included, at any width.
  • Tour into the picture keeps the picture clear: the step's instruction and the handles' words show for a moment, then fade, the still's name sits in the Viewer's bottom right corner, and the plane tool no longer says "No camera" in a mode that makes its own camera.
  • A Kura Write set to PNG 16-bit wrote 8-bit PNGs.
1.0.13 (build 4694)   Nov 16, 2026

New: Tour into the picture

  • One still becomes a room the camera moves through. Projection has a new mode for a single picture, Tour into the picture: right-click a still in the Viewer and choose Tour into this picture, or add a Projection to a still. Five steps, shown on the Viewer's bar and free to jump between: Picture, Room, Things, Fill and Move. Next always names the next thing to do.
  • Room: the room is found from the picture's own straight edges, as the Perspective node finds lines, and drawn over the still at once as a first guess you correct. Drag where the lines meet, a corner of the back wall, or a line's end onto an edge in the picture. A solved Perspective node up the still can seed the room and its lens instead. Click two points and type how long they are to give the room a real size, in meters or feet.
  • Things: click round a thing and it stands where its foot touches, on the floor, hanging from the ceiling or out of a wall. Drag its foot nearer or farther and its top for its height, stand one thing on another, or make one from a Roto shape or a node's alpha.
  • Fill: what the still never showed (behind each thing, and past the picture's edges) is hatched and filled from the pixels around it, so a move that drifts past the edge sees picture, not black. When the room or a thing moves afterward, Fill says it is out of date and offers Fill again.
  • Move: presets named by situation, sliders for push in, drift, rise, turn, tilt, orbit and lens, a map of the room from above, and flying in the Viewer. When the move would see what the picture never showed, a card says where and offers Fill it or Limit the move. Out gives the moving picture at the comp's format; for 3D work, the camera, the room's lines as a Perspective node, and the room and its things as USD or Alembic. In a Nuke script it's offered for baking, with Nuke cameras.

    • New: guided steps on 27 tools

  • Kento's more involved tools now open on a few short steps instead of every control at once. A strip at the top of the panel shows where you are; each step says in one line what to do and shows only its own controls, and Next names the step it goes to. When a step can't go on, an amber line says why with the one button that fixes it ("Couldn't measure: A has too little solid matte", Measure again), and the Viewer's top left shows the same words.
  • All controls, at the strip's right, shows the whole panel as before, with the steps folded above it. Kento remembers your choice for each kind of node, so an artist who knows a tool keeps the full panel.
  • With steps: SmartMerge, HeatHaze, Perspective, Furea, Kiri, ReadSplat, PlateAlign, Grain Match, Nagi, Lens Defocus, DepthGenerator, Isolate, the Lens node, Trainer, RemoveGlare, Matte Refine, ScannedGrain, Clean Plate, MultiMerge, Frame Repair, Position Matte, Create LUT, Prerender, RemoveFlare, Generate and TextureFill. Paint gets a short start checklist instead (what you're painting, the clone source, this frame or every frame) that folds away after the first stroke.
  • A ReadSplat take (a sequence or moving splats) has two more steps once it's in the shot: Playback and Prerender.
  • Perspective's last step, Use, is optional: once the solve is good the panel opens folded to Done.
  • Steps put the right tool in your hand: HeatHaze opens on the Jet or car exhaust preset with the point tool on, so one click where the heat comes from is enough; Perspective's line tool moves to the other direction by itself after two lines; Clean Plate starts with the screen pick on and warns that the default green turns a non-green plate black.
  • A step that needs something else makes it there: Grain Match's Clean step adds a Nagi set up for you, and Lens Defocus's Depth step adds a DepthGenerator, each with its own steps running inside. Steps that need a download (SAM 3.1, the depth, matte and flare models) say so first, with the size, and show the download's progress beside Cancel.
  • Long jobs run in the background with their progress beside Stop: PlateAlign's Track and solve and Align, Kiri's Work out the shot (frames counted, with the time left), Matte Refine, DepthGenerator and RemoveFlare. RemoveFlare, Matte Refine and DepthGenerator show a shot's results when it finishes even if their panel was closed.
  • A click on the picture while a step's tool is on and the Viewer shows another node is refused where you clicked, in a card that fades by itself, with the button that shows the right node.
  • Walking every tool step by step turned up quiet failures, now fixed: Perspective's Camera step asks for the film back (it was folded away, so the focal length came out wrong on most plates without a word); leaving Kiri's Check step puts the Viewer back on Result, so a Matte or Spill view never reaches a render; Create LUT no longer writes a LUT that would change nothing, asks before writing over a file it didn't write, and no longer leaves a Blur switched off after leaving it out of a LUT; ReadSplat's Put in the shot waits for a line-up (it built a network that couldn't line up); the Lens node's lens grid no longer picks the plate itself as the grid; Isolate says when the playhead is outside the tracked frames; Frame Repair says when a word in its list isn't a frame; Prerender's buttons say why they can't start by the button instead of in a dialog.

    • New: buttons you can see

  • Every word you can press (Go to hold, Hold here, Send to paint, Add track, Skip This Version and about 330 more) now has a raised face with a fine light top edge, so it is no longer a guess which words do something. A row's main action is light, ringed in blue; a switch that is on is sunk and lighter; a button that can't be pressed yet keeps its shape, faint. Information, such as a state or a count, stays flat and round. Projection's Best hold... is its row's main action.

    • New: Furea, a flare built from elements

  • Furea's flare is now one stack of elements: the light's core, the iris star, the glow, the veil, the horizontal streak, ghosts traced through a lens, lit dirt, and the rings, iris ghosts, ghost chains and haze you add. Each has its own strength, color, solo, layer and seed, and traced ghosts and drawn ghosts sit in the same flare. A comp saved with an earlier Furea opens as its stack and renders the same.
  • Each element has looks, each a different structure rather than a different strength (the Core's Pinpoint, Sun disc, Lamp and Blown out, for one), measured against the studio's anamorphic and spherical flare footage and reference photographs of its kind of lens. The horizontal streak looks are now the coating's blue rather than white, fading and tapering along their length as real streaks do. Nine new elements: Fine rays, Streak glints, Star filter, Rainbow arc, Tall oval ghost, Lens orbs, Glare rays, Dust specks and Scratches.
  • The twenty presets are now starter flares you can change, and a new Furea opens on the flare you used last. Save flare keeps one for you with its group, tags and a thumbnail; adding it to the studio's library is a separate step that asks what it is for, and the library shows who added each flare and when.
  • The panel is built around the stack: Start from (starters, yours and the studio's, searchable), Light, Whole flare (scale, strength, squeeze, lens, irregularity, flicker), the Elements list (show, solo, strength and drag to reorder on each row) and the chosen element's own rows. In the Viewer, each element has a mark you can drag along the line through the frame's center, and Flare, Solo element and Elements outlined switch what you see.
  • The light is a Point you place in the Viewer, key, or link to a Tracker's track or a CameraTracker's point, or Hotspots found in the picture. Hotspots can merge lights close together into one and cap any one light, so one sun doesn't drown every other light's flare; when no light is as bright as it asks, it lowers the threshold to the brightest light and says so.
  • Traced ghosts can trace a lens of their own (design, focal length and stop) beside the whole flare's, so two lenses' ghosts sit in one flare. List... shows each ghost, brightest first: hide one, or turn it into an Iris ghost you can move freely.

    • Faster

  • A Write no longer waits for movie frames it never uses: Kento decodes a movie's frame only when the render reads its pixels. On a 4.6K comp with a retimed 4K ProRes smoke element (DNK_320), the matte Write beside it went from 0.40 to about 0.20 seconds a frame on a Mac Studio, and the comp's three benchmark Writes now render faster than NukeX 17.1's on the same machine. Writes that do show the movie still have its frames decoded ahead. The pixels are exactly the same.

    • New: AVIF, HEIC and WebP stills

  • A Read opens AVIF, HEIC and WebP stills. On the Mac, macOS's own decoders read them. Wide-gamut photos (Display P3 from a phone) and HDR photos (PQ, HLG, an iPhone photo's HDR rendition) keep their own colors as linear float, read through the config's linear Rec.709 space, so nothing clips; sRGB files read as they are and 10-bit files keep their precision; transparency comes in as a PNG's does, and a photo taken sideways stands upright. The Read's metadata says the file's format, bit depth and profile. Drag them onto the Node Graph, choose them in the file dialog or as Tour into the picture's still, and see them in the Browser's thumbnails. On Windows and Linux, WebP reads; AVIF and HEIC don't yet.

  • A node's button that can't do what was asked now says why in a card under the button that fades by itself, instead of a tip that vanished as the pointer moved: Grain Match's Analyze, Lens Defocus's pick and the other node buttons.     • 1.0.12 (build 4604)   Nov 15, 2026

    Faster

  • A row of Keymixes, as in a defocus made of slices, renders in one pass instead of one pass and a copy for each, and is kept between frames when it doesn't change: MM1_080's main Write renders in about 0.59 s a frame instead of 0.67 on the Mac Studio, the same pixels.
  • RemoveGlare is faster, most with Richardson-Lucy: about a third less time a 4K frame (3.1 to 2.1 s on a busy MacBook Pro), the same picture.
  • Dragging a knob on a heavy comp shows the picture as you drag: the Viewer finishes each picture before it takes the next value, instead of starting over at every move and showing nothing until you let go (POP_010 on a 16 GB Mac mini: no picture during a drag before, one every 1.7 to 2.5 seconds now, about one a second at 1:2). Letting go sets the last value at once.
  • On a Mac with 16 GB of memory or less, Kento starts with smaller caches (image cache 4 GB, playback cache 2 GB), so a long session leaves room for your other apps: on a 16 GB Mac mini a session held about 3 GB less. Settings > Performance shows and changes them as before.
  • Clicking a node in a big comp opens its panel sooner: the Properties panels no longer restyle every open panel at each selection (POP_010 on a 16 GB Mac mini: a click to its panel about 0.8 s before, 0.5 s now).
  • Clicking a knob or stepping to another frame while the Viewer is still working out a big comp's picture no longer freezes the interface until that picture is done: the render engine stops the picture you moved on from at once (POP_010 on a 16 GB Mac mini: a frame step mid-picture held the interface about 1.3 s before, 0.1 s now; a knob click 0.7 s before, 0.06 s now).
  • Stepping through frames the Viewer has already worked out no longer holds up the interface on a big comp: read ahead no longer searches the whole comp at every frame, the Timeline works out its range once a paint, and a Read asks whether its EXR sequence is deep once instead of reading every frame's header (POP_010 on a 16 GB Mac mini: the interface's own time for a step about 0.6 s before, 0.3 s now).
  • Rendering an image sequence, the nodes after a Read no longer work out the picture's size, bounding box and channels again at each new frame when the files' headers are the same: MND_040's main Write gets each frame ready about 0.12 s sooner (0.65 to 0.54 s), the same files.
  • EXR files are written faster: each frame's file is compressed across all of the machine's cores and written in order as its parts are done, and up to three files are written while the next Writes render, so a Write that only copies a plate no longer waits for the file before it (a 4.6K plate copy about 0.08 s to 0.055 s a frame), the same files.
  • A big comp gets each frame ready for the render in about half the time: the parts of a frame's plan that are the same as the frame before are no longer written out and read back again (MND_040's main Write, 1,244 nodes: about 1.4 s to 0.8 s a frame on a busy Mac Studio), the same files.
  • Opening a Nuke script is faster again: each Merge is now one node inside Kento instead of about 45, with the same pixels and the same saved scripts, so a comp with hundreds of Merges opens faster (POP_010 in 1.5 s instead of 3.0 on the Mac Studio, a 1,000-node comp in 1.75 s instead of 2.16). A Keymix is now one node too, and Merges with a driven inject or mix stay one node. A Read, Grade or ColorCorrect builds its view, missing-frame and mix luminance parts only when they are used. A Read is ten nodes lighter inside again, with the same pictures.
  • A run of Grades, Multiplys, Expressions, Clamps, Shuffles, channel copies and matte merges one after another is worked out in one pass on the GPU on a Mac instead of one pass a node, with the same pixels: the ten nodes of an edge-push matte become one, and so do the fifteen of two ChannelMerges with the Invert and Shuffle after them.
  • An Erode (filter) or an EdgeExtend works out only the channels the nodes after it read (an EdgeExtend whose color nothing reads does no fill), a Transform left at its defaults passes its picture through, and a Merge of pictures with different bounding boxes no longer slows down outside the smaller one: a 4K comp that builds an edge matte from a lightwrap (two erodes of its alpha) renders that matte in about a third of the time.
  • Opening a big Nuke script is faster: an expression's text is read once however many nodes share it, and a node's mask and mix are set up only once it is masked or mixed, so a 1,000-node comp opens in about 2.5 s instead of 3.5 on the Mac Studio, the same comp.
  • On a Mac with 48 GB of memory or more, a long render keeps more of its working memory between frames (up to a quarter of the machine's memory, at most 24 GB) instead of asking the system for it again each frame: a heavy 4K comp renders its frames about a quarter faster after the first.
    • A comp whose Writes share most of their nodes (one Write a shuffle or crop of another's picture) works those nodes out once a frame, not once a Write: DNK_100's second Write takes about 0.15 s a frame instead of 0.45, the same files.
    • A Reformat that neither scales nor moves its input (to the format the picture already has, resize none) passes the picture through instead of filtering it: POP_010's 37-channel render passes no longer spend an eighth of a second each on it, the same picture.
    • A Keymix (or any masked node) whose mask is a roto works out its A input only where the mask is above zero, not over the whole frame: PR1_120, whose rotating wheels are motion-blurred Transforms of the 4K plate under small rotos, renders a frame in about 0.15 s instead of 0.8 on the Mac Studio, the same picture.
    • Layered Photoshop files and other decoded copies (PNG, movie frames) are read once per render instead of on every frame, and a masked node reads only its mask's channel: a 4K comp with a layered matte painting and a ProRes movie renders about 1.8 times as fast, the same to the bit.
    • H.264 and HEVC movies decode on the Mac's media engines (VideoToolbox), the same pixels as before; ProRes already decodes there.
    • A ProRes movie Read keeps its decoder open between frames and unpacks frames on every core: a render of frames far apart prepares each new frame's movie frames in about half the time (0.27 s instead of 0.4 for four 4K frames on the Mac Studio), the same pixels.
    • Movie Writes keep the timecode of their first frame (from a Read or AddTimeCode) as a timecode track, as other apps write it.
    • Movie Writes and QuickTime flipbooks encode on the Mac's media engines and prepare their frames on every core: a 4K Write of 24 frames takes 6.6 s instead of 38 in ProRes 4444, and 3.1 s instead of 25 in H.264, with the same codec, profile and color tags.
    • Convolve with an even-sized filter (a Radial or Constant 162 pixels wide, say) now runs on the GPU too: it fell back to the slowest way, about 3 seconds a 4K frame, and now takes about a tenth of a second.
    • Big blurs and their reduced copies use the GPU and every core more often (blurs of 31 taps and up, pictures with values below zero, and the shrink and grow steps of very large blurs), with the same picture as before.
    • Expression nodes run on the GPU on a Mac where they can (color math, comparisons, gammas, clamps; not positions or angles, which keep the CPU's precision).
    • Very large blurs (past their quality) shrink, blur and grow their copy on the GPU on a Mac in one go, the shrunk copy never leaving the GPU; the picture is the same but for an odd value one float step apart.
    • Colorspace to and from CIE-LCH, CIE-Lab and CIE-XYZ (the Photoshop-style blend modes in PSDMerge use them) runs on the GPU on a Mac: a 4K comp with PSDMerge renders about a third faster.
    • PNG Reads with alpha (roto mattes) no longer copy each frame to a temporary TIFF while rendering: the renderer reads the PNG itself, the same picture to the bit. A 4K comp with four roto PNGs renders about 0.15 s a frame faster.
    • A Transform with motion blur sums its samples in one pass on the GPU instead of making a full picture for each: about twice as fast on a 4K plate, the same picture to the bit.
    • Turned and scaled Transforms run on the GPU on a Mac, the same picture to the bit, and motion blur sums its samples faster: a 4K Transform with motion blur renders in about 0.18 s instead of 0.25.
    • EdgeExtend fills on the GPU on a Mac, the same picture to the bit: a 4K EdgeExtend takes about a twentieth of a second instead of a quarter.
    • OCIODisplay, OCIOColorSpace and other OCIO color conversions run on the GPU on a Mac (OCIO's own shader for the conversion, within a half float's step of the CPU's numbers; conversions that use LUT files stay on the CPU for now): a 4K display conversion takes a few milliseconds instead of a tenth of a second.
    • A render reuses what it prepared for frames a comp holds (FrameHold, a held 3D setup) instead of preparing it again on every frame, and prepares the next frame on the Mac's fast cores: MND_040 prepares a frame in about 0.6 s instead of 1.0, the same picture to the bit.
    • 3D scenes hand their triangles to the renderer as packed numbers instead of text: a tracked-geometry comp (MND_040) spends about a third of a second less on each frame, the same picture to the bit.
    • A ReadGeo mesh with its own normals is read in a blink instead of seconds a frame: a 4K comp with tracked 3D geometry (MND_040) prepares each frame about 3 times as fast, the same picture to the bit.
    • ColorCorrect runs on the GPU on a Mac, Grade (the Gaffer kind inside many tools) reads its rows straight, and Erode (filter) uses the GPU for a part of the picture too: a heavy 4K comp such as DNK_320 renders about a fifth faster.

    New

  • Kento seats render for each other on the studio's Tailscale network: each Kento finds the others by itself and lists them in Settings > Rendering and on the Render Queue's new seats line as available, busy, in use or asleep, with no node list to fill in. A new Gently, while I work setting keeps a seat rendering while its artist works, with a few threads, a small cache, low priority and no GPU, and at full speed once they're away; idle now counts the mouse, keys and pen in any app, not only Kento's window.
  • Gaussian splats in the 3D (3D > Geometry > ReadSplat): a splat capture (PLY from a splat trainer, SPZ or .splat) is drawn by ScanlineRender through the comp's camera, on the GPU on a Mac, in depth with cards and meshes and in the Z pass, and shows as colored points in the 3D Viewer.
  • ReadSplat reads splats over time: a take of numbered splat frames (PLY, SPZ, .splat, SOG) conformed to the comp's rate with start at and offset, nearest or held frames, missing frames filled, a read-ahead that follows the playhead within a quarter of the memory free and a half-size frame cache, a frames strip and Timeline band showing what's in memory, and Prerender for playback for smooth review; moving-splat files (.splatv, Spacetime Gaussians PLY) play exactly at any time with real motion blur and their own motion in ScanlineRender's motion vectors, and several can be segments of one take, each segment's numbers keyable.
  • PlateAlign (Transform > Tracking): lines up a take that should have been shot motion control with the master take. Track each plate with its CameraTracker and press Align: the child is lined up in space (from the points both plates show, or the turn alone for cameras on sticks), retimed so each master frame shows its nearest moment, drawn through the master's camera, and each frame's error is graphed. Bake makes a TimeWarp and a CornerPin2D for Nuke.
  • ReadSplat puts a splat capture in the shot: presets for the kind of shot (Phone scan cleanup, Set extension behind the action, Quick layout and more); Keep and Crop drop faint, oversized and floating splats or cap their count, and crop to a box or sphere dragged in the 3D Viewer; Line up fits the cloud to a solved CameraTracker by the points both share or by pairs you pick; scale, ground and origin give the shot its real size; Put in the shot makes the Scene, the render through the tracked camera and the Merge over the plate in one click. Splats are turned from sRGB into the working space, can be drawn as themselves in the 3D Viewer, and ScanlineRender can write them alone to their own layer. Came from names the capture tools (XGrids PortalCam, Nerfstudio, Scaniverse, Postshot and more) and sets their axis; a PortalCam capture's levels and sky are offered, and its cameras.json comes in as Cameras.
  • Lens Defocus (Filter > Blur and defocus): depth defocus with a real lens's bokeh, bright rims in front of focus, cat's eyes toward the frame's edges, color fringes, swirl and anamorphic ovals, from four looks traced from real lenses, with a preview of the bokeh across the frame, Pick in Viewer for the focus, and focus breathing. With DepthGenerator or a render's Z pass; on the GPU.
  • HeatHaze (Filter): heat haze and steam from a simulated flow of hot air, not a noise warp. Pick a preset (hot road, exhaust, fire, desert, candle, steam vent, kettle, manhole steam) and show it the source: a matte, emitters drawn in the Viewer, or the plate's bright areas. Plumes rise, curl and flow around solid things; a depth pass keeps nearer things still. Its outputs: the finished image, an STMap and the steam's density.
  • RemoveGlare (Filter): takes veiling glare, soft flare and haze, and streaks out of a plate. Pick a light and its glare's falloff is drawn with the spread fitted to it (drag the curve's end to widen or narrow it); soft flare is rebuilt from the surroundings, a clean plate or the neighboring frames, the grain kept; streaks are turned on a dial. Removed shows what was taken out, Before and after splits the picture at a line you drag in the Viewer.
  • Furea (Beta: results vary), a lens flare worked out from a lens (Filter > Light and glow): ghosts traced through the glass, a starburst from the iris, veiling glare and dirt on the front glass, with the imperfections a real lens has, set off by a point, a 3D light or the plate's highlights, on the GPU; Designer mode builds one from elements.
  • Furea's presets are temporary (beta): they don't match real flares closely enough yet, and an element library you stack into a flare will replace them in a later Kento. Furea's presets (board 184, revised 15 Nov): one Preset menu of twenty looks in five groups (Daylight, modern glass; Vintage and worn; Anamorphic; Night and practical lights; Graphic and stylized), each a different lens, coating, stop or streak, your own at the foot; Light keeps the preset's optics; Strength (Subtle, Natural, Bold) in place of the Lens type and Genre menus, an old comp's genre shown as its strength. The lens menu is searchable and lists Kento's designs and lenses imported as .lens files (FlareSim's format) into the studio's Furea lens library (Import .lens files...). The star follows the stop; the anamorphic streak's thickness, edges, halo, lines, length and color are controls.
  • Annotations: draw on the Viewer (pen, line, arrow, box, ellipse, text, in seven colors) on one frame or held across a range, with a line of words; they are saved with the comp, show on the Timeline, never reach a render, and go to and from Asobi (a file, its review window) and the shot's Kitsu notes. Bar 2's Annotations button.
  • Annotations read from the shot's Kitsu notes open their Kitsu picture: More > Exchange with Asobi... > Open this annotation's Kitsu picture.
  • A loupe and a navigator in the Viewer: bar 2's loupe button shows the pixels under the pointer enlarged, with their values, and the navigator shows where a zoomed-in view sits in the frame (click or drag in it to move there).
  • Gamut scopes: the Scopes panel adds CIE xy and a gamut view with the working, display and one more gamut drawn, counts the pixels outside the display, and a click on that count marks them in the Viewer.
  • RemoveFlare (Filter, beta: results vary; RemoveGlare for dependable removal): takes a lens flare's ghosts and streaks out of a plate with a learned model (Flare7K++ or FlareX, installed from the panel). Work out the shot once; only the flare is taken from the full-size plate, so grain stays, smoothed across frames so it doesn't flicker, and a farm renders it with no model. Removed shows what was taken; a matte on where keeps it to the flare.
  • DepthGenerator (Other > Models): a depth channel for any plate from a learned model, no camera needed. Work out the shot once, steady across the shot or a frame at a time; near, far and depth (1/z) or distance (z) change instantly, and the farm renders it with no model. The models install from its panel or Settings > AI and MCP > Depth model (about 340 MB on a Mac).
  • Matte Refine has a third solve, learned: a learned model (ViTMatte Small or Base, BiRefNet matting, MatAnyone 2 for steady video, or BackgroundMattingV2 against a clean plate) turns a rough roto or key into an alpha with the hair and edge detail, worked out over the shot in the background and kept beside the comp.   • SmartMerge as a balancer: set result to A matched to B and it gives you the element matched to the plate (levels, color, haze, grain, defocus), premultiplied by its own alpha and not merged, to comp yourself, or to match one CG pass or plate to another. The plate is still what it measures. Light wrap and the operation dim with the reason (the wrap needs the plate behind), mix blends with the element as it came, its tile says "matched only", and Bake to nodes and a saved .nk follow it with no Merge. Tab finds it by "match to plate".

    • Fixed

  • Furea: a light is a crisp core with its rays, streak and ghosts, not a soft round halo. The halo close round a light (the bloom and the near part of the veil) is one control, glow, with glow size, low by default (a quarter of what it was) and up for a glowing look; Sci-fi streak and Energy orb keep theirs. An anamorphic's bloom is small and faint (2 to 3% of the frame's height) and follows the glow. No ghost reads as a second source: ghosts fade out beside the light they come from and stay soft round it; an uncoated lens's are fainter and smaller. Each light gets its own long rays on an anamorphic (never one pattern copied). 1970s single-coated and Sodium street lights throw less ghost wash.
  • Furea's anamorphic presets, from the studio's anamorphic flare footage: a cyan bloom round the core (6 to 8% of the frame's height), a near-vertical spike and one long diagonal ray through the light (uneven, each way its own length), and a wide faint elliptical ring ghost with a rainbow rim across the frame's center from the light. An uncoated lens's ghosts are soft, warm and low in contrast (no hard white disc beside the light); Stage lights in haze no longer shows green smears.
  • Furea, against the studio's own anamorphic flare footage: the streak's lines are soft and one hue (no hard stripes, no separate red, green and blue lines far out), its bright stretches uneven in length, edge and brightness, its segments soft-ended (a gap no longer cuts it with a hard end); a very bright light's streak grows longer and brighter, not into a fat bar; a side row puts the streak to one side of the light. A small light wide open keeps a short spike and a few uneven rays (the star no longer vanishes under f/2.8); Headlights at night has a short streak and rays. Sci-fi streak, Energy orb and Phone camera are resized for full-size frames and the Designer's ring is a soft band. Presets: warm tints on the uncoated ones, uneven spikes on Sunstar and Sun in space, fewer dirt specks; a coating given on a surface stays on an uncoated lens.
  • Render nodes render a knob driven by a Python expression at each frame's own value: the comp sent to a node now carries the expression's values as keys, where before the node held the value from when the job was queued on every frame. A switch or text driven by Python keeps the job on your machine, and the job's log says which knob. Rendering a saved .ko that holds a Python expression from the command line warns that the knob stays at its saved value.
  • Furea's anamorphic streak is back at the scale of real ones and has its own share of the light: it runs across most of the frame (0.85 to 0.94 of the width on the test plates; real ones measured 0.6 to 1.0), as three thin parallel lines leaning cyan, blue and violet, soft-ended segments, pill-shaped bright stretches along it (cyan-white by the light, blue farther out) and a faint wide band; the lavender glow round the core is gone, a tight bloom in the coating's color in its place; streakSide puts it to one side of the light (by script for now). Lights on a dark plate no longer lift the whole frame (the veil's wide part is a sixth of what it was); Stage lights and Flashlight are a third to a half as strong. Designer element sizes follow the frame (their pixels on a 1920-wide one) and a bigger glow is dimmer, not a bigger white ball. The traced ghosts together stay within 1.2% of the light (an uncoated lens washed 4% of it across the frame).
  • Furea's glow no longer blows out: the star, the bloom and the veil each spread a set share of the light (the star a few percent at most, where it laid half the sun's light again round it; the glare half a percent at Veiling glare 1), measured against real flare photographs, so in most presets a sun's white core is 2 to 3% of the frame's width as a photographed sun's is (it was 4 to 7%, and 11 to 13% in Sci-fi streak and Energy orb; ghosts, lit dirt and the anamorphic glow are as they were); the glare is the same from the plate's highlights as from a point; one highlight under a several-light look gets one light's strength; and a light's intensity follows the frame's size, so a preset looks the same on a proxy as at full size (at 1920 across it was 16 times dimmer a pixel than at 480).
  • RemoveGlare's soft flare takes out faint and wide flares with nothing wired into where: a round glow about the light is fitted and taken out (on test plates a faint flare went from 90% left to 8%, a wide one from 27% to 4%, a strong one from 14% to 5%), and a bright box or disc that isn't a flare is left alone.
  • Every number field steps the digit just right of the cursor with Up and Down, as in Nuke (in 110 with the cursor after the first 1, by tens), and a drag pressed on a digit steps by that digit: the older fields some nodes still use now do this too.
  • Saving is reliable on quit: Save all saves every comp under its own name (before, only the front comp was saved, under a new name you were asked for). A comp opened from a .nk saves as the .ko of the same name beside it without asking; a new comp's save dialog names the comp; Save as uses Kento's own save dialog, titled with the comp's name. A save that fails says so, offers Save as, and stops the quit, so no comp is closed with unsaved changes.
  • A Transform that moves its picture by part of a pixel gives the bounding box NukeX gives (its corners grown by one and a half pixels): a stabilized plate keyed and edge-blurred after it no longer ends 60 pixels short of NukeX's box on one side.
  • ZDefocus2 and Bokeh repeat the picture's edge past its bounding box, as NukeX does, instead of blurring in black: no more dark fringe along the frame's edge where the blur reaches out.
  • The Viewer's input process (a node named VIEWER_INPUT) shows again: a Grade or another masked node there had stopped applying to the picture.
  • A Viewer shown through the render engine no longer falls back with a warning when a knob is NaN or infinite (a Constant of NaN, for one).
  • Write's write timecode for movies is a checkbox in its panel: off, a movie has no timecode track even when its input has a timecode.
  • Opening the Scopes panel floating no longer fails with an error since the gamut scopes arrived.
  • Remote control reaches Card2's planes rows: Fold, Extrude, Deal out to cards, Bake and Use the baked textures (card.reshape, card.deal_out, card.bake, card.use_baked).
  • ZDefocus2 (and Bokeh, which uses it) cuts the picture into as many depth layers as NukeX does for its max_size (23 a side at 10, 43 at 20, 54 at 40 and up) instead of at most 12, so blur changes in finer steps across depth: closer to NukeX, at the same speed on the GPU.
  • Window > Panels > Dope Sheet (or any panel) now brings a closed panel back as a tab in its place in the layout, or to the front if it is open; hold Option to float it, and a floating panel has Dock in the main window in its pane menu. Window > Workspaces > Default now also switches the window to that layout.
  • Add a lens from a grid now solves the two-size charts (Cheetos, NBLISS) it used to refuse: lettering inside the squares no longer derails the search, and the small and large squares are solved together with one lens, so all 11 real chart clips solve (the old solve found 3) and the fit reaches the frame's corners instead of extending to them.
  • A render could stop without an error partway through a shot (about one render in eight of a heavy 4K comp) at a node that extends its picture's edges; it no longer does.
    • Gaussian splat files (PLY and the compressed SPZ, versions 3 and 4) can be read, with the picture axes converted to Kento's own.
    • Properties: every choice is a menu now (CopyCat's model size, batch and crop size, Inference's tile size, the older LensDistortion's scaling and output, a Precomp's output Write, a ReadGeo's and Camera's file node, ApplyMaterial's object); readouts such as a time node's frames are words, not boxes; Card's shape, planes and lattice show their own controls; expressions are colored and checked as you type; reference frames and Cryptomatte mattes show as chips with This frame and Add matte; Write's datatype lists EXR's depths before a file is named.
    • A camera made with the Perspective node's Make Camera follows its lines again after the comp is saved and reopened, as a .ko or a .nk; before, it kept its values but stopped following.
    • Perspective's Horizon and forward point now lines up the same direction on both plates, and says when a forward point is too far off the frame to trust; one plate's road could land on the other's cross street.
    • The Perspective panel says when the lines leave the focal uncertain, and when they can't measure it at all it points to From the pictures, which needs no camera.
    • Two Project3D2 nodes through one camera are two projections for occlusion self: one's cards no longer shadow the other's, so Nuke scripts with two projectors open and render as written.
    • Properties: Card's lattice row and Nagi's spatial method row keep inside the panel at its narrowest.
    1.0.11 (build 4344)   Nov 14, 2026

    Fixed

    • In the Viewer, a GridWarp point linked to a Tracker is drawn where the track puts it, and dragging it keeps the link, adding an offset to the track.
    • A GridWarp whose grid points are linked to a Tracker's tracks by expression (as Nuke writes them, Tracker1.tracks.1.track_x) follows the tracker frame by frame, where the render stopped with "isn't a number or a curve".
    • A Write with no channels to write says which Write, at which frame, and why (nothing connected above its chain, or its channels not in what reaches it), where the render said only "No channels to write".
    • IBKColour's patch black fills the black areas with screen color as Nuke does: on a bright blue screen the fill was up to 12 off, now within 0.004.
    • A RotoPaint shape whose Source is the foreground or background (a clone shape) fills with that picture, moved by its translate, as Nuke does, where it drew white; and a RotoPaint or Roto premultiplied in every channel keeps its box to its shapes and strokes instead of the whole frame.
    • An EXR holding only a Y channel reads into red raw, and into red, green and blue through a color space, as Nuke reads it.
    • The Lens panel's Choose another lens menu says Lenses... (it said Stills lenses (lensfun)...), the window it opens, with the studio's lenses first.
    • Add a lens from a grid finds charts with two sizes of square (fine in the middle, coarse at the edges) that it used to refuse with "No grid found".
    • A selected node in the Node Graph keeps its own color, brighter, inside a bold outline you can see at any zoom, instead of going grey with a faint glow. Settings > Node Graph has a new Glow on selected and processing nodes choice: On (glows left out by themselves while the graph is slow to draw), Always, or Off for slower machines.
    • Long frame numbers read and render the right frame: a comp numbered from timecode (86400000 on) read and wrote only every eighth frame, couldn't step one frame on the Timeline and moved keys to every sixth frame. Every frame now reads its own file, renders under its own number, steps, holds and keeps its keys.
    • Long frame numbers in more places: WriteGeo, a camera's or axis's Read file, ReadGeo, GeoImport, DiskCache, Prerender, Precomp and the Flipbook name and read each frame by its own number (86400000 on), and a render started from the Render window or a Flipbook does too.
    • Long frame numbers in Kento's tools: Paint's strokes, the Trainer's pairs and passes, Isolate, Kiri's model mattes, MatchGrade's reference frames and a Projection's hold frame keep and use the frame number you see (86400000 on), and their panels show and go to it.
    • Long frame numbers in more nodes and tools: FrameRepair's bad frames, FlowRetime's frame knobs, Pulldown's cadence, the Off strip and Make keys, SmartMerge, transitions, the GridWarp and SplineWarp tools and the Viewer's time bar all use the frame number you see.
    • Grain, Dither, ScannedGrain, CameraShake3 and FilmLab's grain follow the frame number on long frame numbers: each frame its own grain or shake, the same at a frame however the comp's range is set.
    • The Curve Editor, Dope Sheet, Focus's transport and Bake show and take the comp's own frame numbers on long frame numbers (86400000 on), not numbers counted from the start of the range.
    • Tracking on long frame numbers (86400000 on): the Tracker, PlanarTracker, CameraTracker, Lens solves and bakes, VectorCornerPin's Bake Corners and Roto's track here follow each frame's own picture, keep the frame numbers you see, and their panels step and jump to the right frame.
    • A floating Viewer window can show an input of its own, as a view of the split can: click its title strip to choose it. It stays with the layout and goes back with the view when docked.
    • A comp saved while Viewer2 was shown opens on Viewer2, not an empty Viewer1, and choosing Viewer2 there switches to it.
    • A comp trained before it was first saved now copies the Trainer's passes beside the comp when you save it, and an Inference node made from a pass finds its .cat there, even after the comp and its folder move. A comp with an Inference node in it saves again.
    • On a big comp, a node's processing glow that went steady after one slow redraw starts pulsing again once the Node Graph draws quickly.
    • A ContactSheet whose rows and columns are worked out from how many inputs it has (ceil(sqrt(inputs)) and the like, as studio contact-sheet gizmos set them) lays its grid out from the inputs, instead of the factory 4 by 3.
    • When a node above the Viewer fails, its note in the Viewer's corner stays readable when you switch the Viewer to it (the input's label goes under it), and the card by the node says what went wrong in plain words; a mistake in an expression is named as one.
    • Lit in the 3D view keeps its full detail while you drag an object (Shaded and Textured still draw at half detail until you let go).
    • The CameraTracker's undistort matches NukeX's tracker: the same box (it was 3 to 4 pixels wider; now exact for barrel lenses and any frame shape too), the plate's edge repeated where the lens reads past it (the corners were black), and with lens type Anamorphic its cross terms taken out too (they were ignored); a new cross terms row shows them.
